title: Conditional or Unconditional? A Pre-Registered Cluster-Randomised Design and Cost-Effectiveness Case for Girls' Secondary Stipends in Sindh, Pakistan
abstract: Falsifiable claim. In Sindh, Pakistan, a stipend for girls' secondary schooling that is conditional on 70% attendance raises girls' secondary enrolment by at least 6 percentage points over three years relative to no transfer, and beats an unconditional transfer of equal value by at least 3 percentage points. Falsifier: if the pre-registered cluster-randomised trial returns a conditional-vs-control effect of 0 percentage points or less, or a conditional-minus-unconditional gap below 3 percentage points, the claim that conditionality adds value in Sindh is rejected and the same budget should be paid unconditionally. Why this question, why now. Pakistan has 25.37 million children aged 5–16 out of school, including 13.41 million girls; Sindh alone accounts for 7.82 million out-of-school children, 4.09 million of them girls (Girls Education Statistics and Trends Report 2023–24). Enrolment collapses after primary school — 20.82 million children enrol at primary level but only 9.21 million reach middle school — and in rural Sindh the net enrolment rate for girls at secondary level is 6%. Two rigorous experiments speak directly to the design choice but disagree on what matters: Punjab's Female School Stipend Program, a conditional transfer evaluated by difference-in-differences and regression discontinuity, raised girls' middle-school enrolment by about 9% in relative terms (Chaudhury and Parajuli, 2008, 2010), while a randomised trial in Malawi found the unconditional arm achieved only 43% of the conditional arm's dropout reduction — yet unconditional transfers reduced teenage pregnancy and marriage far more (Baird, McIntosh and Özler, 2011). No experiment has tested conditionality head-to-head in Pakistan. This paper (i) re-uses the published Punjab evaluation to derive a cost-effectiveness benchmark — approximately US$263 per additional girl kept in school for a year (2007 prices) — (ii) scales it transparently to Sindh, and (iii) pre-registers a three-arm cluster-randomised trial (conditional vs unconditional vs control, 240 schools) that settles the question for Sindh's own context. The policy recommendation is conditional on the trial result, not ahead of it. Keywords: conditional cash transfer; girls' education; Sindh; Pakistan; cluster-randomised trial; difference-in-differences; cost-effectiveness; maqasid al-shariah
summary: Falsifiable claim. In Sindh, Pakistan, a stipend for girls' secondary schooling that is conditional on 70% attendance raises girls' secondary enrolment by at least 6 percentage points over three years relative to no transfer, and beats an unconditional transfer of equal value by at least 3 percentage points.

title: Net Billing Made the Battery Pay: A 143-Unit Crossover for Hybrid Solar-plus-Storage in Larkana, Pakistan
abstract: On 9 February 2026, NEPRA replaced Pakistan's net-metering regime with net billing: a household that exports solar electricity is now credited about Rs 8.13 per unit, while the same unit bought back from the grid costs Rs 28–48 depending on the consumption slab. That 4-to-6-fold spread turned the home battery from a luxury into an arbitrage machine — but only for some households. We model a 5 kW rooftop system with a 5 kWh LiFePO₄ battery in Larkana, Sindh (5.0 kWh/kWp/day), using the notified 2026 tariff schedule (S.R.O. 279(I)/2026), the September 2026 fuel charge, and November 2026 market prices (panels Rs 37–47/W; 5 kW on-grid turn-key Rs 700,000–800,000; hybrid premium +Rs 275,000). Falsifiable claim: for an unprotected household, the battery add-on pays for itself within its 10-year warranted life if and only if monthly consumption is at least ~143 units; protected households never cross, at any consumption up to 700 units/month. Falsifier: a metered field trial of 30 Larkana hybrid households showing median marginal battery payback above 10 years at 300–400 units/month, or a NEPRA export rate above ~Rs 25/unit, kills the claim. Causal identification: natural experiment + deterministic cost model — the 9 February 2026 regulatory switch is the treatment; household-level realised paybacks remain to be measured, so no causal effect on adoption is claimed. The memorable number: 143 units/month — the consumption line below which a battery destroys value and above which it creates it (range 117–169 across the observed battery-price range). A 400-unit household earns Rs 35.46 on every unit it stores instead of exporting, pays the battery back in 5.25 years, and gains Rs 401,506 in 25-year net present value over on-grid solar alone. Keywords: rooftop solar; net billing; battery storage; LiFePO₄; NEPRA; Larkana; levelised cost; energy policy; Pakistan
summary: On 9 February 2026, NEPRA replaced Pakistan's net-metering regime with net billing: a household that exports solar electricity is now credited about Rs 8.13 per unit, while the same unit bought back from the grid costs Rs 28–48 depending on the consumption slab.

title: AMG-517 Beats Capsaicin by 2.19 kcal/mol in the Human TRPV1 Vanilloid Pocket — but It Is the Antagonist That Failed in Phase I for Hyperthermia Past 40 °C
abstract: Chronic pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide — about 619 million people lived with low back pain in 2020 — yet the analgesic ladder runs from NSAIDs that fail in neuropathic pain to opioids that carry dependence liability. TRPV1, the capsaicin receptor on pain-sensing nerve endings, is the non-opioid target: capsaicin itself works only topically, as the 8% patch, while every systemic TRPV1 antagonist that reached humans failed — AMG-517 for hyperthermia past 40 °C. We asked whether known antagonists and ChEMBL similarity leads bind the human TRPV1 vanilloid pocket more strongly than re-docked capsaicin. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q8NER1 → ChEMBL CHEMBL4794 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked ten compounds on 8GFA, the 2.29 Å human TRPV1 structure with the antagonist SB-366791, centred exactly on its co-crystallised ligand (centre audit by direct PDB computation — the pipeline's own centre picker lands on a phospholipid 18.4 Å from the pocket). Capsaicin re-docked at −8.26 kcal/mol and SB-366791 self-docked at −9.36 kcal/mol, validating the protocol. AMG-517 scored best at −10.45 kcal/mol, ahead of capsaicin by 2.19, beyond Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise; SB-705498 scored −9.91 and three pipeline leads scored −9.65 to −9.73, all ahead of capsaicin but inside noise. The honest limit: the best binder is the drug that failed in Phase I for fever, the ranking rests on a single antagonist-bound structure, resiniferatoxin failed to dock, and a docking score cannot tell an agonist from an antagonist. The falsifiable next step is a calcium-flux assay of AMG-517 and SB-705498 against capsaicin-evoked human TRPV1 activation, with proton-mode selectivity and core-temperature monitoring: if AMG-517's IC50 is not within 3-fold of SB-705498's published 3 nM, or if it blocks the proton mode as potently as the capsaicin mode, the docking ranking is refuted as a drug lead.
summary: Chronic pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide — about 619 million people lived with low back pain in 2020 — yet the analgesic ladder runs from NSAIDs that fail in neuropathic pain to opioids that carry dependence liability.

title: NMT-C0003 Out-Scores Methotrexate by 0.64 kcal/mol on TbPTR1's 2X9G Structure — but Vina Ranks Pyrimethamine, the Most Potent Measured Inhibitor, Below the Weak Control Cycloguanil
abstract: Human African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness) is near elimination — fewer than 600 cases were reported in 2024, down from nearly 40,000 in 1998 — but the parasite survives in animal reservoirs, and every current treatment can fail. The folate pathway is the weak point that was never fully exploited: the antifolate methotrexate inhibits the parasite's dihydrofolate reductase at 0.040 µM yet is twenty-fold weaker against pteridine reductase 1 (PTR1, IC50 0.793 µM), the NADPH-dependent enzyme that bypasses DHFR inhibition and rescues the parasite. We asked whether any known PTR1 inhibitor binds the enzyme's pterin pocket more strongly than methotrexate. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB O76290 → ChEMBL → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked six literature PTR1 inhibitors on 2X9G, the 1.1 Å co-crystal of TbPTR1 with pemetrexed, centred exactly on the co-crystallised pemetrexed (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). NMT-C0003, the picomolar multitarget inhibitor from Pöhner et al., scored best at −9.74 kcal/mol, ahead of methotrexate at −9.10 kcal/mol by 0.64 — inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise — with pemetrexed self-docking at −9.69 kcal/mol. The honest limit is a rank inversion: pyrimethamine, the most potent measured TbPTR1 inhibitor in the set (IC50 0.090 µM), scored −7.15 kcal/mol, worse than the weak control cycloguanil (IC50 31.6 µM) at −7.56 kcal/mol, and LIB_66 scored worst at −6.92 kcal/mol — the scoring function favours the large folate analogues (MW 427–454) and cannot rank the small diaminopyrimidines (MW 216–252). The falsifiable next step is a single-assay TbPTR1 comparison of NMT-C0003 against methotrexate: if NMT-C0003's IC50 is not better than methotrexate's 0.793 µM under identical conditions, the docking lead is refuted; a parallel DHFR assay must confirm dual inhibition before any parasite work.
summary: Human African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness) is near elimination — fewer than 600 cases were reported in 2024, down from nearly 40,000 in 1998 — but the parasite survives in animal reservoirs, and every current treatment can fail.

title: M2WJ332 Beats Amantadine by 2.74 kcal/mol on the S31N Mutant Channel — but Amantadine's Own 0.49 kcal/mol Drop Cannot Explain Its Resistance
abstract: Seasonal influenza infects around a billion people a year and causes 290,000–650,000 respiratory deaths, and its first antiviral class — the adamantanes, amantadine and rimantadine, which block the influenza A M2 proton channel — is now clinically dead: nearly all circulating seasonal influenza A viruses are resistant, and the US CDC has not recommended adamantanes for years. The resistance is a single amino-acid change, S31N, present in over 95% of adamantane-resistant viruses. We asked whether the published S31N inhibitor M2WJ332 binds the M2 pore more strongly than amantadine on both the wild-type channel and the S31N mutant. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q0HD59 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked amantadine, rimantadine and M2WJ332 on two structures: 3C9J, the 3.5 Å amantadine-bound wild-type channel, and 2LY0, the solution-NMR structure of the S31N mutant bound to M2WJ332 — each centred exactly on its co-crystallised ligand (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). On 3C9J, amantadine self-docked at −6.27 kcal/mol, rimantadine at −6.66 and M2WJ332 at −7.98 kcal/mol. On 2LY0, M2WJ332 scored −8.52 kcal/mol, rimantadine −6.42 and amantadine −5.78 kcal/mol. M2WJ332 therefore beats amantadine by 1.71 kcal/mol on the wild-type channel and by 2.74 kcal/mol on the S31N mutant — both margins beyond Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and consistent with the published plaque assay, where M2WJ332's EC50 against S31N virus (153 nM) beats amantadine's against wild-type virus (328 nM). The honest limit: amantadine's own score falls by only 0.49 kcal/mol between the wild-type and mutant structures, inside the noise, so this docking cannot resolve the resistance it was designed to explain — the published electrophysiology does (amantadine IC50 16 μM wild-type vs 200 μM S31N). The falsifiable next step is a two-electrode voltage-clamp assay of the three compounds on wild-type and S31N M2 under identical conditions: if M2WJ332's S31N IC50 is not within 3-fold of its published 16 μM, the docking ranking is refuted.
summary: Seasonal influenza infects around a billion people a year and causes 290,000–650,000 respiratory deaths, and its first antiviral class — the adamantanes, amantadine and rimantadine, which block the influenza A M2 proton channel — is now clinically dead: nearly all circulating seasonal influenza A viruses are resistant,…

title: AG7404 Beats Rupintrivir on Both HRV 3C Structures — by 0.24 and 0.53 kcal/mol, Inside Vina Noise — and the Covalent Bond Is What the Score Cannot See
abstract: Human rhinoviruses cause most common colds and drive up to 80% of childhood asthma exacerbations, yet no antiviral is approved and no vaccine exists across more than 170 genotypes. The 3C protease, which cleaves the viral polyprotein after glutamine, is the most conserved drug target in the picornavirus family. Its best-characterised inhibitor, rupintrivir (AG7088), is a covalent Michael acceptor that cut symptom scores by 33% in a human challenge trial (mean EC50 0.023 μM across 48 serotypes) and then failed in natural colds, ending development. We asked whether its successors AG7404 and SG85 bind the 3C active site more strongly than re-docked rupintrivir. The automated pipeline first resolved the target wrongly — to the human helicase MDA5 (Q9BYX4) and its structure 3GA3 — so we corrected it by hand and docked all three inhibitors with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on the reference drug's own co-crystal (1CQQ, 1.85 Å) and on the HRV-C15 structure (6KU8, 2.05 Å), each centred on its co-crystallised rupintrivir. Rupintrivir self-docked at −7.45 kcal/mol on 1CQQ and −7.43 on 6KU8, a 0.02 kcal/mol cross-structure difference; AG7404 scored −7.69 and −7.96, ahead on both structures but by 0.24 and 0.53 kcal/mol, inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise; SG85 scored −7.42 on 1CQQ and −7.75 on 6KU8. All three are PAINS-clean, all carry one Lipinski violation, and all fail Veber — large peptidomimetics, as the class's poor oral bioavailability already says. The honest limit is the covalent bond: Vina scores only non-covalent fit, so the reference drug's true binding — which comes largely from irreversible Michael addition to Cys147 — is underestimated by exactly its mechanism of action, and no docking win here can rank this family. The falsifiable next step is a purified HRV 3C FRET enzyme assay under identical conditions: if AG7404's IC50 is not within 3-fold of its published 0.046 μM, or SG85 fails against HRV-C15 3C, the docking ranking is refuted.
summary: Human rhinoviruses cause most common colds and drive up to 80% of childhood asthma exacerbations, yet no antiviral is approved and no vaccine exists across more than 170 genotypes. The 3C protease, which cleaves the viral polyprotein after glutamine, is the most conserved drug target in the picornavirus family.

title: One ChEMBL EZH2 Inhibitor Beats Tazemetostat on Two PRC2 Structures by 1.06 and 1.62 kcal/mol — but Tazemetostat Was Withdrawn in March 2026, So the Win Is a Lead, Not a Successor
abstract: EZH2 is the catalytic subunit of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2, which silences genes by methylating histone H3 at lysine 27; gain-of-function mutations (Y641, A677G, A687V) drive B-cell lymphoma, and the SAM-competitive inhibitor tazemetostat was the first EZH2 drug approved — until Ipsen withdrew it worldwide on 9 March 2026, after the SYMPHONY-1 trial found new blood cancers in 5.7% of treated patients against none in the control arm. We asked whether four ChEMBL EZH2 inhibitors with sub-nanomolar measured potencies bind the SAM pocket more strongly than tazemetostat. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q15910, ChEMBL CHEMBL2189110, AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked the four leads and tazemetostat on two inhibitor-bound PRC2 structures: 5WG6 (3.90 Å, GSK126-bound) and 5IJ7 (2.62 Å, pyridone-bound). The pipeline's first auto-picked structure, 5U5T, was EED, not EZH2, and was rejected by centre audit; a planned 5HYN cross-check failed at receptor preparation and was replaced by 5IJ7. Tazemetostat re-docked at −11.52 kcal/mol on 5WG6 and −12.12 on 5IJ7. One lead, CHEMBL5562984 (measured EZH2 IC50 0.45 nM), beat it on both structures: −12.58 on 5WG6 and −13.74 on 5IJ7, margins of 1.06 and 1.62 kcal/mol, with tight pose consistency on 5IJ7; the other three leads tied or lost, and one flipped from tied to a clear loss between structures. All six compounds are PAINS-clean. The honest limit: the winning margin sits at the edge of Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, the winner is the largest compound in the set, and no docking score can address the second-malignancy risk that ended tazemetostat. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay EZH2 comparison of CHEMBL5562984 against tazemetostat plus a W113C/Y111D mutant panel: if its IC50 is not within 3-fold of tazemetostat's Ki of 2.5 nM, or it fails the resistance mutants, the claim is refuted.
summary: EZH2 is the catalytic subunit of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2, which silences genes by methylating histone H3 at lysine 27; gain-of-function mutations (Y641, A677G, A687V) drive B-cell lymphoma, and the SAM-competitive inhibitor tazemetostat was the first EZH2 drug approved — until Ipsen withdrew it worldwide on 9 Mar…

title: The Preview Census: Rubin's First 7% of the Sky Doubles a Trojan Cloud, Finds Two Galactic Satellites and a 1,000-km World — and the Two Tests That Will Kill the Selection-Effect Model
abstract: Before the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) had even begun, its commissioning and preview data had already rewritten three censuses at once. A preliminary search of the Science Validation survey doubled the known long-term stable Neptune L5 (trailing) Trojans from 2 to 4 (2025 MH348, 2025 NN80; plus candidate 2025 MD138), ending a 15-year drought caused by the cloud sitting behind the Galactic plane (Schwamb et al. 2026). Early Data Preview 2 — about 3,000 deg², 7% of the sky — yielded two new Milky Way satellites, the ultra-faint dwarf candidate Aquarius IV at 109 kpc and the dust-shrouded globular cluster Rubin-GC1 (Cerny et al. 2026; Pai et al. 2026). And a search code run over Rubin data found 2026 ED138, a 600–1,500 km trans-Neptunian object at 46 au — the largest dwarf-planet candidate in roughly twenty years (Rubin Observatory / Minor Planet Center, 27 October 2026). We combine these three results with the first asteroid haul (11,007 new asteroids, 33 new near-Earth objects, ~380 trans-Neptunian objects in six weeks) and derive new numbers: the catalogue under-represents Neptune Trojans relative to Jupiter Trojans by a factor of ~1,800–4,600, and a naive full-sky scaling of the two satellites predicts ~28 more at the same depth (Poisson 95% interval 3–99). Falsifiable claim: all three deficits were selection effects of sky coverage, depth and crowding — not physical deficits. Falsifier: if, by the end of LSST Year 2 (30 June 2028), fewer than 5 additional long-term stable L5 Trojans have been confirmed, or fewer than 10 new ultra-faint Milky Way satellites have been found, the selection-effect model fails and a physical explanation is required. Causal identification: association only — this is a comparative synthesis of published discoveries, not an experiment; the mechanism is instrumental (depth × area × crowding), not astrophysical. The memorable number: 2 → 4 — a preliminary search of a commissioning survey doubled a population that had not grown in fifteen years. Keywords: Vera C. Rubin Observatory; LSST; Neptune Trojans; Milky Way satellites; ultra-faint dwarf galaxies; trans-Neptunian objects; 2026 ED138; survey completeness
summary: Before the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) had even begun, its commissioning and preview data had already rewritten three censuses at once.

title: BI-3406 Self-Docks at −9.07 kcal/mol on Its Own SOS1 Co-Crystal 6SCM — and Beats MRTX0902 and BAY-293 by Less Than Vina Noise
abstract: KRAS is the most commonly mutated oncogene in human cancer, present in about 25% of all tumours — 85–92% of pancreatic cancers, 40–49% of colorectal cancers and 30–35% of non-small-cell lung cancers — and direct KRAS blockade covers only some alleles. SOS1, the guanine-nucleotide exchange factor that switches KRAS from GDP-bound to GTP-bound, sits upstream of all KRAS mutants and is a feedback node that MEK inhibition reactivates, which makes it a combination target. We asked whether the newer SOS1 inhibitors MRTX0902 and BAY-293 bind the SOS1 catalytic pocket more strongly than BI-3406, the reference SOS1::KRAS interaction inhibitor. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q07889 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked BI-3406, MRTX0902 and BAY-293 on 6SCM, the 1.87 Å crystal structure of SOS1 in complex with BI-3406 itself, centred exactly on the co-crystallised BI-3406 (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). BI-3406 self-docked at −9.07 kcal/mol. MRTX0902 scored −8.10 kcal/mol and BAY-293 −8.11 kcal/mol — behind by 0.97 and 0.96 kcal/mol, just inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the two comparators are 0.01 kcal/mol apart. The honest limit: the reference drug wins on its own structure, which biases the comparison in its favour, and BI-3406 itself never entered the clinic — the clinical data belong to its analogue BI 1701963, whose Phase 1 showed limited efficacy as monotherapy (one partial response). The falsifiable next step is a single-assay SOS1::KRAS interaction comparison (IC50) of the three inhibitors under identical conditions: if MRTX0902's IC50 is not within 3-fold of BI-3406's, the dead-heat claim is refuted.
summary: KRAS is the most commonly mutated oncogene in human cancer, present in about 25% of all tumours — 85–92% of pancreatic cancers, 40–49% of colorectal cancers and 30–35% of non-small-cell lung cancers — and direct KRAS blockade covers only some alleles.

title: Etavopivat Out-Scores Mitapivat by 0.09 kcal/mol on the Mitapivat-Bound PKR Structure 8XFD — a Dead Heat Between Two Pyruvate-Kinase Activators, and a 2.74 kcal/mol Gap to the Discontinued Tebapivat
abstract: Beta-thalassaemia is Pakistan's most common inherited blood disorder: 5–8% of the population carries the trait, more than 10 million carriers, about 5,000 children born with thalassaemia major every year, and roughly 100,000 people living with transfusion-dependent disease. Red-cell pyruvate kinase (PKR) activation raises red-cell ATP and lowers 2,3-diphosphoglycerate, a mechanism now validated by mitapivat, approved for pyruvate-kinase deficiency in 2022 and for thalassaemia anaemia in December 2025. We asked whether the newer activators etavopivat and tebapivat bind the allosteric activator pocket more strongly than mitapivat. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P30613 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked mitapivat, etavopivat and tebapivat on 8XFD, the 2.10 Å crystal structure of erythrocyte pyruvate kinase in complex with mitapivat itself, centred exactly on the co-crystallised mitapivat (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). Mitapivat re-docked at −11.06 kcal/mol. Etavopivat scored −11.15 kcal/mol — ahead by 0.09 kcal/mol, a dead heat inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise — while tebapivat scored −8.32 kcal/mol, 2.74 kcal/mol behind mitapivat, a gap larger than the noise. The honest limit: all three are PAINS-clean and Lipinski-compliant, so the difference is not a size or artefact effect, but the scores are rigid-docking numbers on one structure, and mitapivat's own score moves by 0.96 kcal/mol between the erythrocyte structure used here and the liver-isoform structure 7FS3 (−12.02 kcal/mol) — a measure of the method's structural sensitivity. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay PKR activation comparison (EC50) of the three activators under identical conditions: if etavopivat's EC50 is not within 3-fold of mitapivat's, the dead-heat claim is refuted.
summary: Beta-thalassaemia is Pakistan's most common inherited blood disorder: 5–8% of the population carries the trait, more than 10 million carriers, about 5,000 children born with thalassaemia major every year, and roughly 100,000 people living with transfusion-dependent disease.

title: Emavusertib Beats Zimlovisertib by 1.35 kcal/mol on Its Own Co-Crystal 5UIU — but Loses to BAY-1834845 on 6EGE, So the IRAK4 Ranking Is Structure-Dependent
abstract: Interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4 (IRAK4) sits at the bottleneck of Toll-like and interleukin-1 receptor signalling: every MyD88-dependent signal passes through it, and humans born without it die of pyogenic infection in about 43% of cases. Its best-characterised inhibitor, PF-06650833 (zimlovisertib), reached Phase 2 in rheumatoid arthritis and then stopped, with no published reason for its non-advancement. We asked whether the newer IRAK4 inhibitors emavusertib, BAY-1834845 and ND-2158 bind the ATP pocket more strongly than zimlovisertib. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q9NWZ3 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked the four inhibitors on two structures: 5UIU, the 2.02 Å co-crystal of IRAK4 with zimlovisertib itself, and 6EGE, the 1.4 Å structure of IRAK4 with the type I inhibitor DL1 — each centred exactly on its co-crystallised ligand (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). On 5UIU, zimlovisertib self-docked at −9.43 kcal/mol, emavusertib scored −10.78 kcal/mol (ahead by 1.35, beyond Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise), BAY-1834845 −9.81 and ND-2158 −9.23 kcal/mol. On 6EGE the order flipped: BAY-1834845 scored best at −10.29 kcal/mol, emavusertib −10.10, zimlovisertib −9.87 and ND-2158 −9.82 kcal/mol. The honest limit: the reference drug does not win on its own structure, the winner changes with the structure, and emavusertib is the largest compound in the set, so part of its lead is size. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay IRAK4 kinase comparison (IC50) of the four inhibitors under identical conditions: if emavusertib's IC50 is not within 3-fold of zimlovisertib's published 0.2 nM, the 5UIU ranking is refuted.
summary: Interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4 (IRAK4) sits at the bottleneck of Toll-like and interleukin-1 receptor signalling: every MyD88-dependent signal passes through it, and humans born without it die of pyogenic infection in about 43% of cases.

title: LY2409021 Re-Docks at −8.12 kcal/mol on the MK-0893-Bound GCGR Structure 5EE7 — and Rigid Vina Cannot Separate Four Failed Glucagon-Receptor Antagonists
abstract: Type 2 diabetes now affects 589 million adults worldwide, and Pakistan carries the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, with 34.5 million adults affected and 9.3 million undiagnosed. Glucagon-receptor (GCGR) antagonism was a rational strategy against the fasting hyperglucagonaemia of type 2 diabetes, yet every small-molecule antagonist that reached Phase 2 was discontinued, most recently LY2409021, abandoned after hepatic fat and aminotransferase rises. We asked whether any of the four best-known antagonists binds the GCGR antagonist pocket more strongly than LY2409021. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P47871 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked LY2409021, MK-0893, PF-06291874 and LGD-6972 on 5EE7, the 2.5 Å crystal structure of human GCGR in complex with the antagonist MK-0893, centred exactly on the co-crystallised MK-0893 (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). LY2409021 re-docked at −8.12 kcal/mol. MK-0893, the self-dock control, scored best at −8.32 kcal/mol, LGD-6972 at −7.84 and PF-06291874 at −7.46 — the whole class spans 0.86 kcal/mol, inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the reference drug sits 0.20 kcal/mol behind the co-crystallised ligand. The honest limit: all four compounds are large and lipophilic (molecular weights 504–703, logP 5.6–8.8, two Lipinski violations each), so the scores scale with size rather than with the contacts that decide hepatic safety — and the structure is antagonist-bound, so the scores cannot explain why the class failed on liver fat rather than on glucose. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay cAMP inhibition comparison of the four antagonists in the same GCGR-expressing cell line: if the measured IC50 rank order does not match the docking order, the docking rank is refuted.
summary: Type 2 diabetes now affects 589 million adults worldwide, and Pakistan carries the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, with 34.5 million adults affected and 9.3 million undiagnosed.

title: Ambrisentan Scores Worst at −7.37 kcal/mol on the ET-1-Bound ETA Structure 8HCQ — and the Inversion Proves Antagonists Cannot Be Ranked on an Agonist-Bound Structure
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension affects about 25 people per million and is fatal without treatment, yet no endothelin-receptor antagonist has ever been co-crystallised with its target — the first endothelin receptor type A (ETA) structures, solved by cryo-electron microscopy in 2023, hold the agonist endothelin-1, not an antagonist. We asked whether the established endothelin-receptor antagonists bosentan, macitentan, sitaxentan and zibotentan occupy the ETA pocket more strongly than ambrisentan, the most ETA-selective drug in the class. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P25101 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked the five antagonists on 8HCQ, the 3.0 Å cryo-EM structure of ETA bound to endothelin-1, centred on the endothelin-1 residues that occupy the pocket (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). Ambrisentan scored −7.37 kcal/mol — worst in the set. Bosentan scored best at −8.72 kcal/mol, followed by sitaxentan at −8.46, zibotentan at −8.34 and macitentan at −7.57 kcal/mol. The honest limit: the structure is in the active, endothelin-1-bound conformation, so these are pocket-occupancy numbers on an agonist-bound receptor, not antagonist potencies — and the ranking inverts the clinical one, since ambrisentan is the most ETA-selective drug in the set (ETA:ETB about 4,000:1) while the top scorer, bosentan, is the least selective, a dual antagonist. The falsifiable next step is a radioligand binding comparison (Ki) for ETA under identical conditions: if bosentan's Ki is not better than ambrisentan's, the pocket-occupancy ranking is refuted — and the decisive test is an antagonist-bound ETA structure, which does not yet exist.
summary: Pulmonary arterial hypertension affects about 25 people per million and is fatal without treatment, yet no endothelin-receptor antagonist has ever been co-crystallised with its target — the first endothelin receptor type A (ETA) structures, solved by cryo-electron microscopy in 2023, hold the agonist endothelin-1, not…

title: Meropenem Out-Scores Avibactam by 1.22 kcal/mol on Wild-Type OXA-48 — and the Comparison Is Meaningless, Because One Is a Substrate and the Other Is Covalent
abstract: Bacterial antimicrobial resistance directly caused an estimated 1.27 million deaths in 2019, and the OXA-48 carbapenemase — a class D serine β-lactamase widespread in Enterobacterales — is one of the enzymes that makes carbapenems, the drugs of last resort, fail. Avibactam, the diazabicyclooctane inhibitor paired with ceftazidime, inhibits OXA-48 by acylating its catalytic Ser70 — covalently, and only slowly reversibly. We asked whether any measured OXA-48 ligand binds the active site more strongly than avibactam. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q6XEC0 → ChEMBL CHEMBL1287604 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked avibactam and the single ChEMBL ligand with measured potency on the 2.3 Å wild-type OXA-48 structure in covalent complex with avibactam (PDB 4WMC), centred exactly on the co-crystallised avibactam (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). Avibactam re-docked, non-covalently, at −6.73 kcal/mol. The comparator, CHEMBL127 — verified as meropenem, the carbapenem substrate (Kd 850 nM) — scored −7.95 kcal/mol, "beating" avibactam by 1.22 kcal/mol. The comparison is meaningless, and the paper says so plainly: meropenem is the substrate OXA-48 hydrolyses, not an inhibitor, and avibactam's potency lives in the covalent acylation step that rigid non-covalent docking cannot model at all. A substrate out-scoring a covalent inhibitor on a non-covalent score proves the method's limit, not the substrate's superiority. The pipeline's first answer was worse still: it docked both compounds on 8PEB, a directed-evolution quintuple mutant centred on a malonate buffer ion, and those scores are discarded here as measurements of the wrong enzyme. The falsifiable next step is a nitrocefin-hydrolysis inhibition assay of avibactam against OXA-48, with the 4WMC pose as the structural hypothesis — not another docking run.
summary: Bacterial antimicrobial resistance directly caused an estimated 1.27 million deaths in 2019, and the OXA-48 carbapenemase — a class D serine β-lactamase widespread in Enterobacterales — is one of the enzymes that makes carbapenems, the drugs of last resort, fail.

title: Thiolactomycin Re-Docks at −6.92 kcal/mol on Its Own KasA Structure 2WGE — a Weak Binder in the Right Pocket, and a Pipeline That Resolved KasA to a Human Enzyme
abstract: In 2023, tuberculosis caused an estimated 10.8 million new cases and 1.25 million deaths, and Pakistan is among the eight countries accounting for two-thirds of the global burden — yet the front-line drug isoniazid is defeated by katG mutations in most resistant strains, because isoniazid must be activated before it can inhibit its target, InhA. KasA, the β-ketoacyl-ACP synthase of the FAS-II mycolic-acid pathway, is isoniazid-independent: it needs no activation, so a KasA inhibitor bypasses the commonest isoniazid-resistance route entirely. Thiolactomycin, the thiolactone natural product that first proved KasA druggable, inhibits both KasA and KasB, and overexpression of either enzyme raises resistance to it — but no KasA inhibitor has reached the clinic. We asked whether any measured KasA ligand binds the active site more strongly than thiolactomycin. The LeadForge pipeline resolved the target correctly to UniProtKB P9WQD9 (M. tuberculosis KasA, H37Rv) — and then failed twice: ChEMBL resolved to CHEMBL2074, verified live as human maltase-glucoamylase, so zero bioactivities were returned and no comparison set exists; and the pipeline's PDB picker selected 6P9K, KasA in complex with the preclinical indazole JSF-3285, not thiolactomycin — its −6.11 kcal/mol score is a docking into the JSF-3285 pocket and is reported here only as the artefact. On the correct structure, the 1.80 Å crystal structure of KasA with bound thiolactomycin (PDB 2WGE), thiolactomycin re-docked at −6.92 kcal/mol (poses −6.92, −6.88, −5.79) centred exactly on the co-crystallised ligand TLM (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). The paper's finding is therefore a validated control plus two honest negatives: the method recovers binding for the drug in its own pocket, but the score is weak — consistent with a weak, early inhibitor, not with a drug — and the "does any analogue beat thiolactomycin" question cannot be answered from ChEMBL as queried. The falsifiable next step is a KasA enzyme assay of thiolactomycin against its published mechanism, with the 2WGE pose as the structural hypothesis — not another docking run.
summary: In 2023, tuberculosis caused an estimated 10.8 million new cases and 1.25 million deaths, and Pakistan is among the eight countries accounting for two-thirds of the global burden — yet the front-line drug isoniazid is defeated by katG mutations in most resistant strains, because isoniazid must be activated before it ca…

title: Doravirine Re-Docks at −11.85 kcal/mol on Its Own Cryo-EM RT Structure 7Z2G — but the Pipeline's First Answer Was a Protease Structure, and ChEMBL Holds No Comparison Set
abstract: About 40 million people were living with HIV in 2023, and the non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) remain a backbone of antiretroviral therapy — yet the class's history is a history of resistance: K103N alone defeats efavirenz and nevirapine. Doravirine, a pyridinone NNRTI approved in 2018, was designed to keep activity against those mutants, with published IC50 values of 12 nM (wild-type), 21 nM (K103N), 31 nM (Y181C) and 33 nM (K103N/Y181C), and no viral breakthrough in resistance selections at clinically relevant concentrations where rilpivirine and efavirenz both broke through. We asked whether any measured RT ligand binds the NNRTI pocket more strongly than doravirine. The LeadForge pipeline resolved the target to UniProtKB P03366 (Gag-Pol polyprotein) and ChEMBL CHEMBL5823 — and then failed twice: ChEMBL returned zero bioactivities for CHEMBL5823, so no comparison set exists, and the pipeline's PDB picker selected 2HS1, verified live as the 0.84 Å structure of HIV-1 protease (V32I mutant) with darunavir, not reverse transcriptase — its −9.3 kcal/mol "doravirine" score is a docking into the protease active site and is discarded here as meaningless. On the correct structure, the 3.65 Å cryo-EM wild-type RT/DNA complex with doravirine (PDB 7Z2G), doravirine re-docked at −11.85 kcal/mol (poses −11.85, −11.68, −8.16) centred exactly on the co-crystallised ligand 2KW (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). The paper's finding is therefore a validated control plus two honest negatives: the method recovers strong binding for the drug in its own pocket, but the "does any analogue beat doravirine" question cannot be answered from ChEMBL as queried, and the pipeline's structure picker cannot be trusted on polyprotein targets. The falsifiable next step is a wild-type and K103N/Y181C RT polymerase assay of doravirine against its own published IC50s, with the 7Z2G pose as the structural hypothesis — not another docking run.
summary: About 40 million people were living with HIV in 2023, and the non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) remain a backbone of antiretroviral therapy — yet the class's history is a history of resistance: K103N alone defeats efavirenz and nevirapine.

title: PC190723 Re-Docks at −9.43 kcal/mol on Its Own FtsZ Structure 4DXD — but the Pipeline Docked It into the GDP Pocket, and ChEMBL Resolved FtsZ to a Human Enzyme
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus was associated with more than a million deaths in 2019, and methicillin-resistant strains with more than 100,000 deaths directly attributable to resistance — yet no FtsZ inhibitor has reached the clinic. FtsZ, the essential bacterial GTPase that builds the Z-ring at the division site, is the target of PC190723, a 2,6-difluorobenzamide that stabilises FtsZ polymers, suppresses its GTPase activity, and kills staphylococci at a minimum inhibitory concentration of 1 µg/mL against both methicillin-sensitive and methicillin-resistant strains. We asked whether any measured FtsZ ligand binds the interdomain cleft more strongly than PC190723. The LeadForge pipeline resolved the target correctly to UniProtKB P0A029 (S. aureus FtsZ) — and then failed twice: ChEMBL resolved to CHEMBL2074, verified live as human maltase-glucoamylase, so zero bioactivities were returned and no comparison set exists; and the pipeline's PDB picker selected 3VOA, the GDP-form of FtsZ, whose centre is the nucleotide site, not the PC190723 cleft — its −8.83 kcal/mol score is a docking into the GDP pocket and is discarded here as a measurement of the wrong site. On the correct structure, the 2.0 Å crystal structure of S. aureus FtsZ in complex with PC190723 (PDB 4DXD), PC190723 re-docked at −9.43 kcal/mol (poses −9.43, −9.37, −9.16) centred exactly on the co-crystallised ligand 9PC (centre audit via dock._ligand_center, which correctly excluded the 28-atom GDP cofactor in favour of the 23-atom inhibitor). The paper's finding is therefore a validated control plus two honest negatives: the method recovers strong, tight binding for the drug in its own cleft, but the "does any analogue beat PC190723" question cannot be answered from ChEMBL as queried, and the pipeline's structure picker cannot be trusted when a structure holds both a nucleotide and an inhibitor. The falsifiable next step is a GTPase-plus-polymerisation assay of PC190723 against its own published MIC, with the 4DXD pose as the structural hypothesis — not another docking run.
summary: Staphylococcus aureus was associated with more than a million deaths in 2019, and methicillin-resistant strains with more than 100,000 deaths directly attributable to resistance — yet no FtsZ inhibitor has reached the clinic.

title: Two 0.01 nM BCL-2 Inhibitors Dock 0.90 kcal/mol Apart and Venetoclax Sits in the Middle: Rigid Vina Cannot Rank the BH3-Mimetic Series on 8HTS
abstract: Venetoclax, the first-in-class BCL-2-selective BH3 mimetic approved in 2016, transformed chronic lymphocytic leukaemia — yet continuous single-agent treatment leaves up to 50% of heavily pre-treated patients refractory after two to three years, most often through BCL2 mutations such as G101V and D103Y that disrupt drug binding while preserving native BH3 binding. We asked whether any measured BCL-2 ligand binds the BH3 groove more strongly than venetoclax. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P10415 → ChEMBL CHEMBL4860 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked venetoclax and four ChEMBL ligands with measured potency on the 1.25 Å BCL-2 structure 8HTS, centred exactly on the co-crystallised sonrotoclax-series ligand S-10r (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). Venetoclax re-docked at −10.22 kcal/mol. Two analogues beat it: CHEMBL3973960 at −11.04 kcal/mol (Ki 0.013 nM) and CHEMBL3985475 at −10.88 kcal/mol (Ki 0.01 nM) — but the margins, 0.82 and 0.66 kcal/mol, lie inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. The decisive failure is the ranking itself: the two most potent compounds by assay (both Ki 0.01 nM — CHEMBL3985475 and CHEMBL4228713, the latter verified as A-1211212) docked at −10.88 and −9.98 kcal/mol, 0.90 kcal/mol apart, while a 1.3-fold weaker compound (CHEMBL3973960, Ki 0.013 nM) scored best of all at −11.04 kcal/mol. Docking therefore cannot rank this series, and no analogue can be claimed to beat venetoclax on this evidence. The honest limit: the whole class is large and hydrophobic (molecular weights 868–910, logP 8.1–9.4, three Lipinski violations each), so the scores scale with size and hydrophobic surface rather than with the specific contacts that decide G101V resistance — and the structure used is wild-type BCL-2, so the resistance question was not docked at all. The falsifiable next step is a fluorescence-polarisation binding assay of the two best-scoring analogues against venetoclax on wild-type and G101V BCL-2 — not another docking run.
summary: Venetoclax, the first-in-class BCL-2-selective BH3 mimetic approved in 2016, transformed chronic lymphocytic leukaemia — yet continuous single-agent treatment leaves up to 50% of heavily pre-treated patients refractory after two to three years, most often through BCL2 mutations such as G101V and D103Y that disrupt drug…

title: The Metabolic Price of Sanity: Xanomeline–Trospium and the Nine-Year Life Gap in Schizophrenia — A Quantitative Synthesis and a Head-to-Head Trial Design
abstract: Question. Schizophrenia affects about 27 million people worldwide, and they die roughly nine years earlier than the general population — mostly of cardiovascular and metabolic disease, much of it driven by the weight gain their own medicines cause. Xanomeline–trospium (Cobenfy), approved by the US FDA on 26 September 2024, is the first antipsychotic in more than three decades that does not block dopamine — it stimulates M1/M4 muscarinic receptors instead — and it causes weight loss rather than weight gain. We asked whether the published evidence supports moving it from a last-resort option for heavily pre-treated patients to a first-line treatment, and what trial would settle the question. Claim. Pooling the published EMERGENT programme, xanomeline–trospium beats placebo by 9.9 PANSS points (95% CI −12.4 to −7.3; Cohen's d 0.65; n = 640) with a number needed to treat of 5 for a ≥30% symptom response, while patients lose a mean 2.2–2.6 kg over 52 weeks — against olanzapine's +4.15 kg in 10 weeks, a metabolic swing of at least 6.8 kg. Real-world claims data (n = 2,613) show 65.5% persistence at month 5, but 49% of initiators were already on three or more antipsychotics, so the drug has not yet been tested as first-line treatment in practice. We therefore pre-specify the trial that would settle it: a randomised, double-blind, head-to-head non-inferiority trial against aripiprazole in first-episode psychosis, powered on a 5-point PANSS margin (n ≈ 205 per arm; ≈ 840 with the 51% attrition the EMERGENT-5 trial observed), with 52-week weight change as the co-primary superiority endpoint. Falsifier. If that trial shows xanomeline–trospium inferior to aripiprazole by ≥5 PANSS points, or a 52-week weight advantage under 1 kg, the first-line claim fails. Identification. Randomised, placebo-controlled evidence for efficacy and for short-term weight change; association only for the claim that weight neutrality closes the mortality gap — no trial has yet linked an antipsychotic's weight profile to survival. One clean number: 9 years — the life-expectancy gap that is, in large part, a metabolic gap. Keywords: schizophrenia; xanomeline–trospium; Cobenfy; muscarinic agonist; antipsychotic; weight gain; cardiometabolic risk; first-episode psychosis; health equity
summary: Question. Schizophrenia affects about 27 million people worldwide, and they die roughly nine years earlier than the general population — mostly of cardiovascular and metabolic disease, much of it driven by the weight gain their own medicines cause.

title: Aliskiren Re-Docks at −8.78 kcal/mol on Its Own Renin Structure — and a 0.039 nM Analogue Scores −10.01, but a Second Equally Potent Analogue Docks Identically to Aliskiren
abstract: Hypertension affects 1.3 billion people and one in three adults worldwide, yet four in five are not adequately treated, and the only approved direct renin inhibitor, aliskiren, failed to improve outcomes when added to ACE-inhibitor or ARB therapy in the ALTITUDE trial. We asked whether structure-based docking can rank renin inhibitors by potency, using aliskiren as the reference and the ChEMBL renin bioactivity set as the lead pool. The pipeline resolved human renin (UniProtKB P00797) to ChEMBL CHEMBL286, retrieved 54 bioactivities, and ranked 26 leads; docking ran on two structures — 2V0Z (renin co-crystallised with aliskiren, 2.2 Å) and 3K1W (renin co-crystallised with a different inhibitor, 1.50 Å). On 2V0Z, aliskiren self-docked at −8.78 kcal/mol, CHEMBL1276275 (IC50 0.039 nM) scored −10.01, 1.23 kcal/mol better, while CHEMBL3907708 (also IC50 0.039 nM) scored −8.79, 0.01 kcal/mol from aliskiren despite being about 15-fold more potent in assay. On the cross-dock structure 3K1W, aliskiren fell to −6.84 and CHEMBL3907708 to −7.51. Three further top leads, each with 17–18 rotatable bonds, could not be docked at all: their Vina runs did not converge in 9–11 minutes on this machine and were terminated without a score. Docking therefore ranks this series only partially and only on the self-dock structure, and a single Vina score is not a reliable potency predictor. The falsifier is a head-to-head renin enzymatic assay of aliskiren, CHEMBL1276275 and CHEMBL3907708 under identical conditions: if the 0.039 nM compounds do not outperform aliskiren there, the docking claim fails.
summary: Hypertension affects 1.3 billion people and one in three adults worldwide, yet four in five are not adequately treated, and the only approved direct renin inhibitor, aliskiren, failed to improve outcomes when added to ACE-inhibitor or ARB therapy in the ALTITUDE trial.

title: DSM265 Self-Docks at −10.70 kcal/mol on Its Own PfDHODH Structure — but Two Weaker Analogues Score Better, and the Ranking Inverts
abstract: Malaria caused 263 million cases and 597,000 deaths in 2023, three-quarters of the deaths in children under five in Africa, and artemisinin resistance makes new antimalarials urgent. DSM265, a selective Plasmodium falciparum dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (PfDHODH) inhibitor, is the reference compound for this benchmark. We asked whether Vina docking on the DSM265-bound PfDHODH structure ranks known PfDHODH inhibitors by their measured IC50 values. The pipeline resolved PfDHODH (UniProtKB Q08210) to ChEMBL CHEMBL3588732, retrieved 58 bioactivities, and ranked 26 leads; docking ran on 4RX0 (PfDHODH co-crystallised with DSM265, 2.25 Å) and on 7L01 (PfDHODH co-crystallised with a different inhibitor, DSM782, 1.6 Å). On 4RX0, DSM265 self-docked at −10.70 kcal/mol, but CHEMBL3289670 (IC50 35 nM) scored −12.16 and CHEMBL1738786 (IC50 38 nM) scored −11.86 — both weaker in assay than DSM265 (IC50 27 nM) yet better in docking, so the ranking inverts. The same molecule docked twice under different SMILES spellings scored −10.70 and −10.37 on 4RX0 and −8.22 and −7.79 on 7L01, a same-molecule reproducibility spread of 0.33–0.43 kcal/mol, and the self-dock structure scored every compound about 2.5 kcal/mol better than the cross-dock structure. Docking therefore cannot rank this PfDHODH series, and the best-pose scores are unstable across poses. The falsifier is a head-to-head PfDHODH enzymatic assay of DSM265, CHEMBL3289670 and CHEMBL1738786 under identical conditions: if the two analogues do not outperform DSM265 there, the docking ranking is refuted.
summary: Malaria caused 263 million cases and 597,000 deaths in 2023, three-quarters of the deaths in children under five in Africa, and artemisinin resistance makes new antimalarials urgent.

title: Sotorasib Self-Docks at −8.71 kcal/mol on Its Own KRAS G12C Structure — but Vina Scores Only the Non-Covalent Pose, and the 4.77 kcal/mol Cross-Dock Spread Is a Pocket Artefact
abstract: KRAS was considered undruggable for decades until covalent inhibitors of the G12C mutant reached the clinic; sotorasib received FDA accelerated approval on 28 May 2021, with a 37.1% objective response rate in CodeBreaK 100. We asked whether Vina docking on the sotorasib-bound KRAS G12C structure ranks known KRAS G12C inhibitors by their measured potency. The pipeline resolved KRAS (UniProtKB P01116) to ChEMBL CHEMBL2189121, retrieved 51 bioactivities, and ranked 26 leads; docking ran on 6OIM (KRAS G12C covalently bound to sotorasib, 1.65 Å) and on 9IAY (GDP-KRAS in complex with a different inhibitor, 0.953 Å). On 6OIM, sotorasib self-docked at −8.71 kcal/mol and the four analogues scored −8.20 to −9.21, a 1.01 kcal/mol spread for compounds spanning 0.3–0.6 nM — docking cannot separate them. On the cross-dock structure 9IAY the spread exploded to 4.77 kcal/mol, with sotorasib worst at −7.54 and an analogue best at −12.31. The cross-dock spread is a pocket artefact, not a potency signal, and Vina cannot model the covalent bond to Cys12 that gives these drugs their potency, so every score here is a non-covalent pose score only. The falsifier is a covalent docking or free-energy calculation (or a head-to-head biochemical assay with fixed pre-incubation time) of sotorasib, CHEMBL5892737 and CHEMBL5905084 under identical conditions: if the covalent-aware ranking does not separate the 0.3 nM compound from the 0.6 nM compound, the docking approach is confirmed uninformative for this series, and future KRAS G12C work must use covalent-aware methods from the start.
summary: KRAS was considered undruggable for decades until covalent inhibitors of the G12C mutant reached the clinic; sotorasib received FDA accelerated approval on 28 May 2021, with a 37.1% objective response rate in CodeBreaK 100.

title: Upadacitinib Re-Docks at −9.30 kcal/mol on the Tofacitinib-Bound JAK1 Structure — but the Ranking Reverses on a Second JAK1 Structure, and Docking Cannot Decide Whether Any Measured Analogue Beats It
abstract: Question. Rheumatoid arthritis is projected to affect 31.7 million people by 2050, and upadacitinib — a JAK1-selective inhibitor that beat adalimumab in the SELECT-COMPARE trial (ACR20 71% vs 63% at 12 weeks) — costs over $60,000 a year for uninsured patients. We asked whether any compound with measured JAK1 potency already in ChEMBL binds the JAK1 ATP pocket more strongly than upadacitinib. Claim. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P23458 → ChEMBL CHEMBL2835 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked upadacitinib and five ChEMBL ligands (IC50 0.011–0.031 nM) on the 1.90 Å tofacitinib-bound JAK1 structure 3EYG, centred exactly on the co-crystallised tofacitinib (centre audit via dock._ligand_center), and confirmed the result on the 1.33 Å JAK1 structure 6N7A. On 3EYG upadacitinib re-docked best at −9.30 kcal/mol, 0.39 ahead of the best analogue. On 6N7A the ranking reversed: three analogues beat upadacitinib (−9.63, −9.56 and −9.24 vs −8.41 kcal/mol), a 1.39 kcal/mol swing for the same compound between structures. Docking therefore cannot rank this series, and no analogue can be claimed to beat upadacitinib on this evidence. Tofacitinib, the pan-JAK incumbent, re-docked worse than upadacitinib on both structures (−7.87 and −8.10 kcal/mol). All five analogues share tofacitinib's pyrrolo-pyrimidine core, pass Lipinski/Veber with no PAINS alerts, and carry only low Tox21 read-across signals. Falsifier. A JAK1 binding assay showing an analogue's Kd worse than its published IC50, or an IL-6-stimulated STAT3-phosphorylation cell assay showing no advantage over upadacitinib, refutes the claim for that compound. Identification. Validated-control re-docking on two co-crystal structures; association only beyond that — docking scores are not activity. One clean number: 1.39 kcal/mol — the swing in one compound's docking score between two JAK1 structures, larger than the 0.39 kcal/mol gap it was supposed to settle. Keywords: JAK1; upadacitinib; tofacitinib; rheumatoid arthritis; molecular docking; ChEMBL; Janus kinase; selectivity
summary: Question. Rheumatoid arthritis is projected to affect 31.7 million people by 2050, and upadacitinib — a JAK1-selective inhibitor that beat adalimumab in the SELECT-COMPARE trial (ACR20 71% vs 63% at 12 weeks) — costs over $60,000 a year for uninsured patients.

title: Sofosbuvir Re-Docks at −9.23 kcal/mol on Its Own NS5B Structure — but the Most Potent Analogue and a 13-Fold Weaker One Dock Identically, and Docking Cannot Rank This Series
abstract: An estimated 50 million people live with chronic hepatitis C, which caused about 242,000 deaths in 2022, and Pakistan carries an estimated 12.6 million of the combined hepatitis B and C burden — yet the cure exists: direct-acting antivirals clear the virus in over 95% of patients in 8–12 weeks. Sofosbuvir, the nucleotide NS5B polymerase inhibitor at the centre of those regimens, was launched at US$84,000 for a 12-week course against an estimated manufacturing cost of US$68–136, and its only well-documented resistance substitution, S282T, confers just 2- to 18-fold reduced susceptibility. We asked whether any measured NS5B ligand binds the polymerase active site more strongly than sofosbuvir. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q8JXU8 → ChEMBL CHEMBL5375 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked sofosbuvir and four ChEMBL ligands with measured potency on the 2.9 Å sofosbuvir-diphosphate-bound NS5B structure 4WTG, centred exactly on the co-crystallised sofosbuvir diphosphate (centre audit via dock._ligand_center), with the RNA primer/template kept in the receptor. Sofosbuvir re-docked at −9.23 kcal/mol with tight pose consistency. No analogue beat it: the best analogue scored −8.94 kcal/mol, a 0.29 kcal/mol margin inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. The decisive failure is the ranking itself: the most potent analogue by assay (CHEMBL5815143, EC50 53 nM) and a 13-fold weaker one (CHEMBL6047888, EC50 690 nM) docked at −8.90 and −8.94 kcal/mol — 0.04 kcal/mol apart — while the weakest compound in the set (CHEMBL109569, IC50 2,250 nM) scored worst at −7.62 kcal/mol. Docking therefore cannot rank this series, and no analogue can be claimed to beat sofosbuvir on this evidence. The honest limit: the docked sofosbuvir is the parent prodrug, while the crystal holds its diphosphate metabolite and the active form in cells is the triphosphate GS-461203; and the ChEMBL ligands have no annotated binding site, so a non-nucleoside inhibitor in the set may bind the thumb or palm allosteric site ~35 Å away, where an active-site score means nothing. The claim that any analogue beats sofosbuvir would be refuted if an NS5B polymerase assay shows an IC50 worse than the analogue's published value. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week NS5B polymerase-plus-replicon assay of the two best-scoring analogues against sofosbuvir, including the S282T mutant.
summary: An estimated 50 million people live with chronic hepatitis C, which caused about 242,000 deaths in 2022, and Pakistan carries an estimated 12.6 million of the combined hepatitis B and C burden — yet the cure exists: direct-acting antivirals clear the virus in over 95% of patients in 8–12 weeks.

title: The HBV Polymerase Benchmark Cannot Run: No Experimental Structure, No ChEMBL Target — and What the Organism-Level Data Say About Tenofovir
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B infects an estimated 254 million people and killed about 1.1 million in 2022, yet only 13% of those infected have been diagnosed and 3% treated — and Pakistan alone carries an estimated 12.6 million of the combined hepatitis B and C burden. Tenofovir is the first-line nucleos(t)ide analogue, but it rarely achieves a functional cure because covalently closed circular DNA persists in hepatocytes, and long-term therapy selects resistance mutations. We asked whether any measured anti-HBV compound binds the viral polymerase more strongly than tenofovir, using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem/RDKit → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7) with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate as the reference drug. The benchmark cannot run, and this paper documents exactly why: the pipeline's first run resolved the target to the wrong protein entirely — human RNA helicase DDX3X (UniProtKB O00571) — and its corrected run resolved the true target, HBV Protein P (UniProtKB P03156, genotype D, 832 amino acids), but ChEMBL holds no single-protein HBV polymerase target, and the pipeline's fallback then silently selected an unrelated human target (ABCC9, CHEMBL1971), whose 41 bioactivities were discarded. No experimental high-resolution structure of HBV polymerase exists — the only structural record is a 14.5 Å cryo-EM density of the encapsidated enzyme — so docking was skipped rather than run on a substitute. The usable evidence is organism-level: ChEMBL target CHEMBL613497 (Hepatitis B virus) holds 3,659 potency records with pChEMBL values across 2,513 molecules, topped by entecavir (IC50 0.06 nM in dHepaRG cells) and tenofovir (EC50 0.064 nM in HepG2.2.15 cells) — but those two numbers come from different assays and the tenofovir value sits far below the published micromolar range for the same cell line, so no head-to-head ranking can be built on them. The honest limit: no docking score exists in this paper, no analogue can be claimed to beat tenofovir, and the claim that the benchmark is impossible would be refuted by the deposition of a single high-resolution HBV polymerase structure with a bound inhibitor. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week validation of an AlphaFold-based HBV polymerase model against the published deep-mutational-scanning fitness map, followed by a HepG2.2.15 antiviral assay of the best-scoring tenofovir analogues.
summary: Chronic hepatitis B infects an estimated 254 million people and killed about 1.1 million in 2022, yet only 13% of those infected have been diagnosed and 3% treated — and Pakistan alone carries an estimated 12.6 million of the combined hepatitis B and C burden.

title: Multi-target computational triage of known bioactive chemical space against seven disease targets: similarity screening, ADMET/toxicity read-across and AutoDock Vina docking (week of 16–22 Nov 2026)
abstract: We screened the bioactive chemical space of ChEMBL against seven therapeutically relevant targets in one week of automated LeadForge runs (16–22 Nov 2026): Escherichia coli DNA gyrase GyrB, HIV-1 protease, hepatitis C virus NS5B polymerase, E. coli cell-division protein FtsZ, Plasmodium vivax dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) and human PI3K-alpha (PIK3CA). For each target, the reference drug was recovered from live ChEMBL data (rediscovery check), 1–50 known ligands were similarity-screened (P. vivax DHFR: a single measured bioactivity in ChEMBL), leads were ranked on a composite of similarity, Lipinski/Veber drug-likeness, PAINS and kNN toxicity read-across, and the top five leads were docked with AutoDock Vina against the best available X-ray structure, with the reference drug re-docked as control. Two runs produced leads that docked clearly better than their reference drug: GyrB (four leads, best −8.06 vs −6.91 kcal/mol for novobiocin) and P. vivax DHFR (CHEMBL5270166, −9.33 vs −7.98 for pyrimethamine — a scaffold hop, Tanimoto 0.081, measured IC50 94 nM). Two runs were marginal wins inside Vina noise (HIV-1 protease, ~0.5 kcal/mol; FtsZ, 0.42–0.56 kcal/mol). Three runs were honest negatives on docking (NS5B, PLpro top-5, PIK3CA) — but the PLpro run still surfaced a genuine lead outside the ranked top-5: CHEMBL6151243, with a measured PLpro IC50 of 1.0 nM (~2000-fold more potent than GRL0617 in vitro) and a docking score 0.20 kcal/mol better than the GRL0617 re-dock. Two runs caught and corrected structure-selection errors before reporting (PLpro: Mpro-dominated auto-pick; PIK3CA: an HLA peptide-presentation structure auto-picked instead of the enzyme). All findings are computational triage; no compound is claimed as a drug, and wet-lab validation is required.
summary: We screened the bioactive chemical space of ChEMBL against seven therapeutically relevant targets in one week of automated LeadForge runs (16–22 Nov 2026): Escherichia coli DNA gyrase GyrB, HIV-1 protease, hepatitis C virus NS5B polymerase, E.

title: Who Gets the Youth Loan? Concentration, Subsidy and the Missing Enterprise Test in Pakistan's PMYBALS, 2023–2026
abstract: Question. Pakistan's Prime Minister's Youth Business & Agriculture Loan Scheme (PMYBALS) has disbursed roughly Rs 289 billion since January 2023 to over half a million borrowers, at a taxpayer subsidy the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) prices at about 15 paisa per rupee lent. Its stated purpose is youth enterprise creation. Does the money actually reach young entrepreneurs and create new enterprises — or does subsidised credit concentrate in a small number of large borrowers while youth unemployment keeps rising? Claim. On the published aggregates, the scheme fails its own enterprise test twice over. First, concentration: in the SBP's own tier tables to December 2025, Tier-III loans (Rs 1.5–7.5 million, 7% fixed interest) took 67.0% of all money disbursed while reaching only 11.0% of borrowers, and the average Tier-III loan (Rs 2.92 million) was 22 times the average interest-free Tier-I loan (Rs 132,339) that 85.6% of borrowers received. Second, no enterprise signal: while Rs 175 billion had been disbursed by June 2025, youth unemployment (ages 15–24) rose from 11.1% (2020-21) to 12.6% (2024-25) in the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics Labour Force Survey, and the 27.4% jump in SECP company registrations in FY2024-25 is attributed by SECP itself to digitisation (99.9% of incorporations online), not to the loan scheme. A third finding is a data-quality failure: the press-reported claim that Rs 102 billion went to 3,957 agriculture borrowers is arithmetically impossible under the scheme's Rs 7.5 million loan cap (maximum Rs 29.7 billion) — a 3.4× gap that the government has not explained. Falsifier. The claim is refuted if either (i) district-level SBP disbursement data, once published, show that per-youth disbursement positively predicts per-youth SECP registrations or Labour Force Survey youth self-employment after controlling for the pre-2023 registration trend and the SECP digitisation rollout, or (ii) a follow-up survey of a random sample of Tier-I borrowers finds that at least 50% operate a business that was still trading 24 months after disbursement. The FY2026-27 outturn — a Rs 292 billion disbursement target that exceeds the entire three-year cumulative total — is the first scheduled test. Identification. Association only. This is a descriptive audit of published national aggregates, with no control group and no randomised or quasi-experimental variation in who receives loans. Confounders — SECP digitisation, GDP growth, inflation, the January 2023 scheme launch coinciding with post-flood recovery lending — are named, not controlled. The paper falsifies the claim that "disbursement equals enterprise creation"; it does not estimate a causal effect of any loan. A difference-in-differences design on district-level data and a randomised musharakah-vs-interest-loan trial are proposed as the causal tests. One clean number: 67% of the money to 11% of the borrowers — the share of PMYBALS disbursements absorbed by the largest loan tier, against 85.6% of borrowers sharing 23.7% of the money in the interest-free tier. The stakes number is Rs 38 billion: the SBP's estimated annual subsidy bill for the scheme, against Rs 21 billion budgeted — a Rs 17 billion (45%) funding gap. Keywords: PMYBALS; youth enterprise; credit concentration; subsidy; Pakistan; SBP; SECP; riba; musharakah; 'adl; maqasid.
summary: Question. Pakistan's Prime Minister's Youth Business & Agriculture Loan Scheme (PMYBALS) has disbursed roughly Rs 289 billion since January 2023 to over half a million borrowers, at a taxpayer subsidy the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) prices at about 15 paisa per rupee lent.

title: Deucravacitinib Re-Docks at −10.19 kcal/mol on Its Own TYK2 JH2 Structure — but the Pipeline First Docked the Wrong Domain, and Three Analogues Lead by Less Than Vina Noise
abstract: Psoriasis affects an estimated 2–3% of the world's population, and its most effective oral drug, deucravacitinib, is the first medicine that works by binding the pseudokinase (JH2) domain of tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) rather than the conserved ATP site — yet it clears the skin completely in only about one in seven patients, and a next-generation rival has just beaten it head to head. We asked whether any measured TYK2 ligand binds the JH2 pocket more strongly than deucravacitinib itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P29597 → ChEMBL CHEMBL3553 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked deucravacitinib and four ChEMBL ligands with measured potency on the 2.35 Å deucravacitinib-bound TYK2 JH2 structure 6NZP, centred exactly on the co-crystallised deucravacitinib (centre audit via dock._ligand_center), and confirmed the result on the 2.73 Å JH2 structure 6NZH. Deucravacitinib re-docked at −10.19 kcal/mol on its own structure and −10.38 kcal/mol on 6NZH. Three analogues out-scored it on best pose on 6NZP — CHEMBL5419627 at −10.62, CHEMBL4789639 at −10.50 and CHEMBL4435170 at −10.46 — but every margin (0.27–0.43 kcal/mol) lies inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the ranking contradicts measured potency: the most potent ligand by assay (CHEMBL5424497, Kd 0.019 nM) docks worst on both structures, while the least potent (CHEMBL5419627, Kd 0.028 nM) docks best on 6NZP. The ranking is also not stable to structure choice: on 6NZH deucravacitinib is best and CHEMBL4435170 is worst, a 1.84 kcal/mol swing for the same compound. Docking therefore cannot rank this series, and no analogue can be claimed to beat deucravacitinib on this evidence. The honest limit: the pipeline first docked the wrong domain (the JH1 ATP site, 3LXP) and that run is discarded; all five potencies span only 0.019–0.028 nM, so the set cannot test ranking at all; and no laboratory data exist for any compound in this study. The claim that any analogue beats deucravacitinib would be refuted if a TYK2 JH2 binding assay shows a Kd worse than the analogue's published value. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week JH2 binding-plus-cell assay of the best-scoring analogue against deucravacitinib.
summary: Psoriasis affects an estimated 2–3% of the world's population, and its most effective oral drug, deucravacitinib, is the first medicine that works by binding the pseudokinase (JH2) domain of tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) rather than the conserved ATP site — yet it clears the skin completely in only about one in seven patien…

title: TAM16 Re-Docks at −9.82 kcal/mol on the Pks13 Thioesterase Domain — but the Pipeline First Docked the Wrong Domain, Every Compound Carries a PAINS Alert, and the Most Potent Analogue Docks Worst
abstract: Tuberculosis caused 10.8 million cases and 1.25 million deaths worldwide in 2023, and Pakistan carries 6.3% of that burden — about 670,000 cases in 2024, the fifth-highest national total — yet no approved drug targets polyketide synthase 13 (Pks13), the enzyme that performs the final step of mycolic-acid synthesis for the mycobacterial cell wall. The best-known Pks13 inhibitor, the benzofuran TAM16, matched isoniazid in mouse models of tuberculosis in 2017 and then stalled, in part over cardiotoxicity concerns. We asked whether any measured Pks13 ligand binds the thioesterase domain more strongly than TAM16 itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB I6X8D2 → ChEMBL CHEMBL4105939 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked TAM16 and four ChEMBL analogues with measured potency on the 1.98 Å Pks13 thioesterase structure 5V3Y, centred exactly on the co-crystallised TAM16 (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). TAM16 re-docked at −9.82 kcal/mol. No analogue beats it beyond noise: the best, CHEMBL5070158 at −9.68, trails by 0.14 kcal/mol, and the most potent by assay (CHEMBL5074531, IC50 180 nM) docks worst at −8.69. The same molecule entered twice (TAM16 as query and as ChEMBL4443524) scores 0.25 kcal/mol apart — the representation noise of the method — which is larger than any analogue margin in the table. Every compound in the set, including TAM16 itself, carries a PAINS alert for its aminomethyl-phenol Mannich-base motif, which the validation design must control for. The honest limit: the pipeline first docked the wrong domain (the ACP domain, 6C4Q) and that run is discarded; all five potencies span only 180–330 nM; and no laboratory data exist for any compound in this study. The claim that any analogue beats TAM16 would be refuted if a Pks13 thioesterase assay shows an IC50 worse than TAM16's 190 nM. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week enzyme-plus-MIC test of the best-scoring analogue against TAM16, with PAINS controls.
summary: Tuberculosis caused 10.8 million cases and 1.25 million deaths worldwide in 2023, and Pakistan carries 6.3% of that burden — about 670,000 cases in 2024, the fifth-highest national total — yet no approved drug targets polyketide synthase 13 (Pks13), the enzyme that performs the final step of mycolic-acid synthesis for…

title: Belzutifan Re-Docks at −10.94 kcal/mol on the Belzutifan-Bound HIF-2α Structure — but Two Analogues Lead by Less Than Vina Noise and the Least Potent Compound Docks Best
abstract: Kidney cancer caused 434,840 new cases and 155,953 deaths worldwide in 2022, and most clear-cell renal cell carcinomas are driven by loss of the von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) tumour suppressor, which leaves hypoxia-inducible factor 2-alpha (HIF-2α) permanently switched on — yet only one drug, belzutifan, directly inhibits HIF-2α, and it works in only a minority of advanced cases. We asked whether any measured HIF-2α ligand binds the drug's own PAS-B pocket more strongly than belzutifan itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q99814 → ChEMBL CHEMBL1744522 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked belzutifan and four ChEMBL analogues with measured potency on the 2.75 Å belzutifan-bound HIF-2α–ARNT structure 7W80, centred exactly on the co-crystallised belzutifan (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). Belzutifan re-docked at −10.94 kcal/mol, a strong self-dock control. Two analogues out-scored it on best pose — CHEMBL5723338 at −11.40 and CHEMBL4453227 at −11.22 — but both margins (0.46 and 0.28 kcal/mol) lie inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the ranking contradicts measured potency: the best-docking analogue is the least potent by assay (IC50 16.0 nM), while the most potent (EC50 4.0 nM) docks second and belzutifan itself (IC50 9.0 nM) docks last. On median pose the order scrambles again, with CHEMBL4173075 leading by 0.33 kcal/mol. Docking therefore cannot rank this scaffold series, and no analogue can be claimed to beat belzutifan on this evidence. The honest limit: the structure is the mouse heterodimer (no human belzutifan-bound HIF-2α structure exists), all five compounds share one scaffold, and no laboratory data exist for any compound in this study. The claim that any analogue beats belzutifan would be refuted if a TR-FRET HIF-2α–ARNT dimer-disruption assay shows a Ki worse than belzutifan's 20 nM. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week TR-FRET plus luciferase-reporter test of the two best-scoring analogues against belzutifan.
summary: Kidney cancer caused 434,840 new cases and 155,953 deaths worldwide in 2022, and most clear-cell renal cell carcinomas are driven by loss of the von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) tumour suppressor, which leaves hypoxia-inducible factor 2-alpha (HIF-2α) permanently switched on — yet only one drug, belzutifan, directly inhibits HI…

title: Fasiglifam Re-Docks at −10.23 kcal/mol on the GPR40–MK-8666 Structure — but One Analogue Leads by 1.71 kcal/mol, the Most Potent Analogue Docks Worst, and Every Analogue Is More Lipophilic Than the Drug That Failed on Liver Safety
abstract: Pakistan has the highest age-standardised diabetes prevalence in the world — 31.4% of adults, about 34.5 million people, with 9.3 million undiagnosed — and type 2 diabetes is therefore the country's largest chronic-disease burden. GPR40 (free fatty acid receptor 1, FFAR1) is an attractive target because it potentiates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, so it lowers blood glucose with a low risk of hypoglycaemia; but its best-known agonist, fasiglifam (TAK-875), was terminated in late phase 3 in December 2013 over liver safety, and no GPR40 agonist has reached the market since. We asked whether any measured GPR40 agonist binds the receptor's allosteric pocket more strongly than fasiglifam itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB O14842 → ChEMBL CHEMBL4422 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked fasiglifam and five ChEMBL analogues with measured potency on the 2.20 Å GPR40 structure 5TZR, centred exactly on the co-crystallised partial agonist MK-8666 (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). Fasiglifam re-docked at −10.23 kcal/mol. One analogue, CHEMBL3287571, leads by 1.71 kcal/mol on best pose (−11.94) and 1.43 kcal/mol on median pose — the first lead beyond Vina noise in this series — but the ranking contradicts measured potency: the most potent analogue by assay (CHEMBL4463571, EC50 0.2 nM) docks worst at −9.71, and fasiglifam itself (EC50 0.35 nM) docks second-worst. Every analogue is more lipophilic than fasiglifam (logP 5.02–6.79 vs 5.31), the property class that drove fasiglifam's liver injury through bile-acid transporter inhibition and a reactive acyl glucuronide. The claim that any analogue beats fasiglifam would be refuted if a GPR40 functional assay shows an EC50 worse than fasiglifam's, or if a bile-acid transporter panel shows inhibition at therapeutic concentrations. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week functional-plus-safety test of the best-scoring analogue against fasiglifam, with transporter and mitochondrial controls.
summary: Pakistan has the highest age-standardised diabetes prevalence in the world — 31.4% of adults, about 34.5 million people, with 9.3 million undiagnosed — and type 2 diabetes is therefore the country's largest chronic-disease burden.

title: Capmatinib Re-Docks at −12.11 kcal/mol on Its Own c-MET Structure — but No Analogue Beats It Beyond Vina Noise, and the Same Molecule Scores 0.38 kcal/mol Apart by Encoding Alone
abstract: Lung cancer caused an estimated 2.5 million new cases and 1.8 million deaths worldwide in 2022, and about 3–4% of non-small-cell lung cancers (NSCLC) are driven by MET exon 14 skipping — yet the first selective drug for that lesion, capmatinib, still fails most patients who receive it second-line, and resistance mutations in the kinase domain defeat it outright. We asked whether any measured MET ligand binds the c-MET kinase domain more strongly than capmatinib itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P08581 → ChEMBL CHEMBL3717 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked capmatinib and four ChEMBL ligands with measured potency on the 1.2 Å c-MET kinase structure 4R1V, centred exactly on the co-crystallised pyridazinone inhibitor (centre audit 0.00 Å), and confirmed the result by self-docking capmatinib and the best analogue on the 1.32 Å wild-type c-MET–capmatinib structure 9SXJ. Capmatinib re-docked at −11.80 kcal/mol on 4R1V and −12.11 kcal/mol on its own structure 9SXJ. The best analogue, CHEMBL3582305, leads by 0.37 and 0.37 kcal/mol on the two structures — both margins inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise — and its measured IC50 (0.13 nM) is identical to capmatinib's, so there is no pharmacological difference for docking to explain. The decisive control is accidental: capmatinib appears twice in the set, once as the PubChem query and once as ChEMBL3188267, and the two encodings of the same molecule score 0.38 kcal/mol apart — exactly the size of the largest "analogue advantage" in the table. Docking therefore cannot rank this series, and no analogue can be claimed to beat capmatinib on this evidence. The honest limit: all five compounds are near-equipotent by assay (IC50 0.13–0.4 nM), so the set cannot test ranking at all, and no laboratory data exist for any compound in this study. The claim that any analogue beats capmatinib would be refuted if a MET kinase assay shows an IC50 worse than capmatinib's 0.13 nM. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week kinase-plus-cell assay of the best-scoring analogue against capmatinib, including the D1228/Y1230 resistance mutants.
summary: Lung cancer caused an estimated 2.5 million new cases and 1.8 million deaths worldwide in 2022, and about 3–4% of non-small-cell lung cancers (NSCLC) are driven by MET exon 14 skipping — yet the first selective drug for that lesion, capmatinib, still fails most patients who receive it second-line, and resistance mutati…

title: Two Tarbelas a Year: The Post-2015 Acceleration of Indus Basin Groundwater Loss and a Stepped-Wedge Groundwater Budget for Punjab
abstract: Question. Has Indus Basin groundwater loss genuinely accelerated since 2015, is the acceleration driven by pumping rather than climate, and what policy, tested how, would stop it in Pakistan's Punjab? Claim. Yes, the loss more than tripled: basin-wide terrestrial water storage fell at −0.65 cm/yr in 2002–2015 and at −2.16 cm/yr after 2015 (Dharpure et al., Water Resources Research, 2025). Converted to volume over the basin's 1.12 million km², that is a rise from ~7 km³/yr to ~24 km³/yr — about twice the design live storage of Tarbela Dam, every year.
