The acceleration is pumping-driven and concentrated in managed landscapes: non-glaciated regions lose water about twice as fast as glaciated ones (−1.44 vs −0.78 cm/yr), downscaled GRACE attributes 47–83% of the decline in most sub-regions to anthropogenic stressors, and aquifer depletion drives 67% of the Indus's total water-storage decline. Pakistan alone extracts ~65 km³/yr of groundwater against ~55 km³/yr of recharge — a ~10 km³/yr deficit, roughly one Tarbela a year. Falsifier. The claim fails if (i) GRACE-FO data for 2024–2028 show the non-glaciated/glaciated loss ratio collapsing toward 1 (which would mean the acceleration is climate-driven, not pumping-driven), or (ii) a stepped-wedge trial of district groundwater budgets shows no divergence between pilot and control districts after five years (see §6). Either result would require withdrawing the pumping-driven attribution or the policy, respectively. Identification. Natural-experiment contrast (glaciated vs non-glaciated regions under shared climate forcing; managed vs natural landscapes in downscaled GRACE) plus a general additive model decomposition for attribution; the attribution is association only — not causal proof. The policy claim will be tested by a stepped-wedge cluster-randomised rollout of district groundwater budgets, which is the causal design. One clean number: 24 km³/yr — the water the Indus Basin now loses every year, about two Tarbelas. The stakes number is 300 million: the people the basin supports. Keywords: Indus Basin; groundwater depletion; GRACE; GRACE-FO; Punjab; tube wells; solar pumping; stepped-wedge trial; khilafah; water commons.
summary: Question. Has Indus Basin groundwater loss genuinely accelerated since 2015, is the acceleration driven by pumping rather than climate, and what policy, tested how, would stop it in Pakistan's Punjab? Claim.

title: Cabozantinib Out-Docks Selpercatinib on Wild-Type RET (7DUA) by 0.65 kcal/mol — a Margin Inside Vina Noise That Contradicts a 27-Fold Measured Potency Gap
abstract: RET fusions drive 1–2% of non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancers and RET point mutations drive most medullary thyroid cancers; selpercatinib, the selective RET inhibitor, produced objective responses in 62–83% of RET fusion-positive lung cancers in the final LIBRETTO-001 analysis, yet acquired resistance through solvent-front G810 and hinge Y806 mutations is inevitable. We asked whether the older multikinase inhibitors that selpercatinib replaced, or its selective sibling pralsetinib, bind wild-type RET more strongly than selpercatinib itself. Because ChEMBL's activity endpoint returned HTTP 500 on the study date, no ChEMBL ligand set could be retrieved; instead we docked five literature-known RET inhibitors with published potencies — selpercatinib, pralsetinib, cabozantinib, vandetanib and the 7DUA co-crystallised ligand HJ0 — on the 1.64 Å human RET kinase structure 7DUA with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, centred on the co-crystallised ligand (chain A centroid, independently verified). Cabozantinib scored best at −10.76 kcal/mol, ahead of HJ0 (−10.27), selpercatinib (−10.11), pralsetinib (−9.98) and vandetanib (−9.55), with no PAINS alert in any compound; selpercatinib's score reproduced within 0.10 kcal/mol across three independent re-docks. The honest limit: the 0.65 kcal/mol cabozantinib margin lies inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the docking order contradicts the measured potency order — cabozantinib is 27-fold weaker than selpercatinib biochemically (11 nM versus 0.4 nM) — with a Spearman rank correlation of −0.32 between docking scores and published biochemical IC50 values. The claim that rigid docking can rank RET inhibitors would be refuted if free-energy refinement (MM-GBSA) on the same five compounds recovered the measured potency order with Spearman rho above 0.8, and the decisive next step is a single-assay biochemical kinase panel of the four drugs against wild-type and G810S RET.
summary: RET fusions drive 1–2% of non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancers and RET point mutations drive most medullary thyroid cancers; selpercatinib, the selective RET inhibitor, produced objective responses in 62–83% of RET fusion-positive lung cancers in the final LIBRETTO-001 analysis, yet acquired resistance through solv…

title: No Parasite Structure for Atovaquone's Qo Site: the Y268S Resistance Gap, a PubChem Analogue Set, and the Qi-Site Escape Route
abstract: Malaria killed an estimated 597,000 people in 2023, and in Pakistan cases peaked at 2.7 million that year after the 2022 floods; atovaquone, the Qo-site inhibitor of the parasite mitochondrial cytochrome bc1 complex, remains a mainstay of prophylaxis and treatment in combination with proguanil, but a single cytochrome b mutation, Y268S, raises its inhibitory constant 270-fold and its whole-parasite IC50 by up to about 9,000-fold. We asked whether any ChEMBL-recorded or PubChem-similar Qo-site ligand could out-perform atovaquone against the parasite enzyme. The LeadForge pipeline verified the target (UniProtKB Q02768, ChEMBL CHEMBL1777), but the ChEMBL activity endpoint returned HTTP 500 for control targets on 2026-11-20, so the enzyme-level activity count could not be verified and the pipeline's empty result is not reported as a finding. A PubChem fastsimilarity_2d search returned 30 analogues of atovaquone; the five retaining the 4-hydroxy-1,2-naphthoquinone core were profiled with RDKit, and the closest drug-like analogue (CID 71768) matches atovaquone's hydrogen-bond counts and polar surface area with a lower logP (4.96 versus 5.35) and zero Lipinski violations, but no measured potency is attached to any analogue. Docking was not performed: no experimental structure of the Plasmodium falciparum bc1 complex exists — the only atovaquone-bound bc1 structure is yeast (PDB 4PD4, 3.04 angstrom). Every analogue, like atovaquone itself, carries a PAINS quinone alert. The literature's escape route is the Qi site: ELQ-300 retains full potency against Y268S parasites and, combined with atovaquone, cured murine malaria at a single 1 mg/kg dose. The claim that a new Qo-site ligand beats atovaquone would be refuted if it loses potency against purified Y268S bc1 enzyme or fails to bind a validated Pf Qo-site model; the falsifiable next step is a homology-model screen of the five analogues against wild-type and Y268S Pf cytochrome b, tested in a bc1 inhibition assay.
summary: Malaria killed an estimated 597,000 people in 2023, and in Pakistan cases peaked at 2.7 million that year after the 2022 floods; atovaquone, the Qo-site inhibitor of the parasite mitochondrial cytochrome bc1 complex, remains a mainstay of prophylaxis and treatment in combination with proguanil, but a single cytochrome…

title: The Fosfomycin Benchmark Is Broken: Non-Covalent Docking Cannot Rank MurA Inhibitors When the Reference Drug Is Covalent
abstract: Fosfomycin is the only clinically used inhibitor of MurA, the first enzyme of bacterial peptidoglycan synthesis, and it works by a covalent bond to the active-site cysteine Cys115 — a mechanism no non-covalent docking score can price. We asked whether ChEMBL-recorded MurA inhibitors and published non-covalent leads genuinely out-bind fosfomycin, or whether the comparison itself is broken. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P0A749 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL1984 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on the 1.7 Å Escherichia coli MurA structure 3KQJ, grid centred on the co-crystallised UDP-N-acetylglucosamine), we re-docked fosfomycin and eight candidates on identical settings. Fosfomycin's non-covalent score is only −5.04 kcal/mol, yet its measured ChEMBL IC50 is 100 nM; seven of eight candidates out-score it, the best by 5.83 kcal/mol (CHEMBL5219133, −10.87 kcal/mol), and the most potent measured non-covalent inhibitor, ampelopsin (480 nM), scores −8.65 kcal/mol. The ranking is inverted against measured potency (Spearman ρ = −0.37, n = 6): the two best dockers are the weakest measured inhibitors (4.5–4.8 µM), and both carry logP 6.5–7.0 with two Lipinski violations. The honest limit is that a Vina score cannot rank a covalent drug against non-covalent candidates, the margins exceed Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise only because the benchmark is meaningless, and the two flavonoid leads carry PAINS alerts. The claim that any candidate beats fosfomycin would be refuted if a MurA enzyme assay shows an IC50 above 50 µM, or if the candidate fails against the fosfomycin-resistant C115D mutant. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week enzyme-plus-MIC test of the two best dockers and ampelopsin against wild-type and C115D MurA.
summary: Fosfomycin is the only clinically used inhibitor of MurA, the first enzyme of bacterial peptidoglycan synthesis, and it works by a covalent bond to the active-site cysteine Cys115 — a mechanism no non-covalent docking score can price.

title: Asundexian Re-Docks at −9.05 kcal/mol on the Milvexian-Bound Factor XIa Structure — but the First Approved FXIa Inhibitor Still Leaves the Decisive Question Open
abstract: Stroke killed 6.8 million people in 2023, yet every anticoagulant that prevents it also causes the bleeding it is meant to avoid — and the first drug designed to break that trade-off has just split its own evidence in two. Asundexian, an oral factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor, failed its atrial-fibrillation trial (OCEANIC-AF: stroke or systemic embolism 1.3% vs 0.4% on apixaban, hazard ratio 3.79) but succeeded as add-on therapy after noncardioembolic stroke (OCEANIC-STROKE: ischaemic stroke 6.2% vs 8.4%, hazard ratio 0.74, no increase in major bleeding) and was approved by the US FDA on 9 November 2026 — the first FXIa inhibitor approved anywhere. We asked whether asundexian and its closest chemical analogues bind the true FXIa active site more strongly than the co-crystallised inhibitor milvexian. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P03951 → ChEMBL CHEMBL2820 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked asundexian, four PubChem analogues and milvexian on the 0.92 Å FXIa structure 7MBO, centred exactly on the co-crystallised milvexian (centre audit 0.00 Å). Asundexian re-docked at −9.05 kcal/mol with tight pose consistency (−9.05, −9.04, −8.89), no PAINS alert, and one Lipinski violation (molecular weight 593). Two of four PubChem analogues out-scored it on best pose — 135205642 at −10.03 and 135205940 at −9.88 — but both margins (0.98 and 0.83 kcal/mol) lie inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the first is a single-pose outlier whose other poses (−8.99, −8.89) tie or trail asundexian; the other two scored −9.19 and −8.99. The decisive check is the self-dock control: milvexian, the co-crystallised ligand of this structure and the more potent drug by measured Ki (0.11 nM vs 0.26 nM), re-docked worst at −7.83 kcal/mol — 1.22 kcal/mol behind asundexian. Docking therefore ranks this scaffold family inversely to measured potency, and no analogue can be claimed to beat asundexian on this evidence. The honest limit: ChEMBL's activity endpoint returned HTTP 500 all day, so the analogues carry no measured potency and the comparison is structural, not pharmacological; no laboratory data exist for any compound in this study. The claim that any analogue beats asundexian would be refuted if a chromogenic FXIa enzyme assay shows a Ki worse than asundexian's 0.26 nM. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week enzyme-plus-aPTT test of the two best-scoring analogues against asundexian and milvexian.
summary: Stroke killed 6.8 million people in 2023, yet every anticoagulant that prevents it also causes the bleeding it is meant to avoid — and the first drug designed to break that trade-off has just split its own evidence in two.

title: The 8-Chloro Isomer of Alisertib Out-Docks Alisertib on the 1.96 Å Aurora A Structure — but the 0.33 kcal/mol Margin Is Inside Vina Noise and the Most Potent Measured Inhibitor Docks Ninth
abstract: Aurora kinase A (AURKA) is amplified or overexpressed in many solid tumours, yet no Aurora kinase inhibitor is approved anywhere: alisertib, the most advanced, failed its Phase 3 LUMIERE trial in peripheral T-cell lymphoma (response rate 33% versus 45% for the comparators). We asked whether alisertib analogues or other clinical-stage AURKA inhibitors bind the true ATP pocket more strongly than re-docked alisertib. ChEMBL's bioactivity endpoint was down on the day of the run (HTTP 500 for every target), so the comparison set was built from PubChem 2D-similar analogues of alisertib plus four literature inhibitors with published potencies, and docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on the 1.96 Å AURKA structure 6C2R at the co-crystallised LY3295668 centroid. The best score came from PubChem CID 92044531, the 8-chloro positional isomer of alisertib, at −9.20 kcal/mol versus −8.87 for alisertib and −8.95 for the co-crystallised LY3295668; two further analogues scored −8.77 and −8.74, and the two top-similarity hits turned out to be sodium-salt forms of alisertib itself. The honest limit: the 0.33 kcal/mol margin is inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, the most potent measured inhibitor (MK-5108, IC50 0.064 nM) docked ninth of ten at −8.19, the docking–potency correlation across the five literature compounds is weak (Spearman rho 0.40, p = 0.51), and no analogue carries a measured potency. The claim that the 8-chloro isomer is a better AURKA inhibitor would be refuted if a biochemical kinase assay shows its IC50 more than 10-fold worse than alisertib's 1.2 nM, or if cellular phospho-Thr288 inhibition shows no advantage. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week kinase-plus-cellular test of the isomer against alisertib and LY3295668.
summary: Aurora kinase A (AURKA) is amplified or overexpressed in many solid tumours, yet no Aurora kinase inhibitor is approved anywhere: alisertib, the most advanced, failed its Phase 3 LUMIERE trial in peripheral T-cell lymphoma (response rate 33% versus 45% for the comparators).

title: One Hydrogen Atom in Thirty-One: The Deuterium Ladder of Interstellar Comets and a Two-Population Test for the Rubin Era
abstract: Three interstellar objects have now passed through the Solar System — 1I/'Oumuamua (2017), 2I/Borisov (2019) and 3I/ATLAS (2025) — and the third has finally given us isotopes. JWST/NIRSpec spectra of 3I/ATLAS (22–23 December 2025, r_H ≈ 2.4 au) measured a methane D/H ratio of (3.18 ± 0.30)% — the highest methane D/H ever measured anywhere, 13 ± 2 times the Rosetta value at comet 67P — and a water D/H of (0.98 ± 0.06)%, more than an order of magnitude above any known comet, with ¹²C/¹³C ratios of 141–191 (CO₂) and 123–172 (CO). We compile the complete isotopic record of all three interstellar objects against the Solar System comet baseline and derive four new numbers: 3I/ATLAS water is 63× Vienna Standard Mean Ocean Water (VSMOW) and 18.5× the water of 67P; its methane is 204× VSMOW; its CH₄/H₂O D/H ratio (3.24) matches 67P's (4.6) within a factor of 1.4, implying the same deuteration mechanism operating ~13–18× harder; and on every measured axis — D/H, ¹²C/¹³C, CO/H₂O — both active interstellar comets sit outside the entire Solar System comet range. Falsifiable claim: interstellar comets fall into two formation populations — a Cold-Core population (water D/H ≥ 0.3%, ¹²C/¹³C > 120) and a Warm-Disk population (water D/H ≤ 0.05%, ¹²C/¹³C < 100) — with almost no objects in between. Falsifier: a single future measurement of an interstellar comet's water D/H inside the 0.05–0.3% gap band, or a cold-band D/H paired with ¹²C/¹³C < 100, kills the two-population model. Causal identification: association only — this is a comparative synthesis of published observations, not an experiment; the mechanism is physico-chemical (H₂D⁺ ion–molecule deuteration at T ≲ 30 K; ¹³C as a secondary nucleosynthesis product whose Galactic abundance grows with time). At the Rubin Observatory's expected discovery rate (0.9–1.9 interstellar objects per year), the test is decidable by the very next cometary interstellar object with a measured water D/H. The memorable number: 3.18% — one hydrogen atom in every thirty-one in 3I/ATLAS's methane is deuterium. Keywords: interstellar comets; 3I/ATLAS; deuterium; isotopic ratios; JWST; Rubin Observatory; planet formation; Galactic chemical evolution
summary: Three interstellar objects have now passed through the Solar System — 1I/'Oumuamua (2017), 2I/Borisov (2019) and 3I/ATLAS (2025) — and the third has finally given us isotopes.

title: Four Sub-Nanomolar RIPK1 Ligands Bind the Allosteric Pocket at −8.6 to −9.9 kcal/mol — but They Are One Chemotype, and the Drug Already Failed in Rheumatoid Arthritis
abstract: Receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) drives necroptosis and inflammatory cytokine production, and its first-in-class inhibitor GSK2982772 reached Phase 2 — then failed to show meaningful clinical improvement in rheumatoid arthritis. We asked whether ChEMBL-recorded RIPK1 ligands bind the allosteric pocket more strongly than GSK2982772 itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q13546 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL5464, 46 bioactivities → PubChem/RDKit similarity, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked the top four leads and GSK2982772 on the 2.0 Å human RIPK1 kinase-domain structure 7FD0, centred on the co-crystallised benzoxazepinone inhibitor (verified centroid). All four leads scored −8.57 to −9.90 kcal/mol against −9.80 kcal/mol for re-docked GSK2982772, with tight pose consistency; their measured IC50 values are 0.4–0.79 nM, and none of the 26 pipeline leads carries a PAINS alert. The honest limit: the best lead (CHEMBL4071864, −9.90 kcal/mol) is GSK2982772 itself, the other three are close analogues of the same benzoxazepinone-triazole chemotype, every margin over the reference is inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the reference drug already failed its efficacy test in patients despite on-target exposure. The claim that any of these analogues is a better RIPK1 drug would be refuted if a kinase assay shows no potency advantage over GSK2982772, or if a cellular necroptosis assay shows no advantage. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week kinase-plus-necroptosis test of the three analogues against GSK2982772, with a brain-penetration screen — the indication where RIPK1 inhibition still has an open question.
summary: Receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) drives necroptosis and inflammatory cytokine production, and its first-in-class inhibitor GSK2982772 reached Phase 2 — then failed to show meaningful clinical improvement in rheumatoid arthritis.

title: Avibactam and Durlobactam Tie at −6.5 kcal/mol on OXA-23 — but the Scores Are Non-Covalent Only, and the Only Sub-Nanomolar ChEMBL Ligand Is a Boronate Vina Cannot Score
abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) sits atop the WHO critical-priority list, and in most of the world its carbapenem resistance is OXA-23 — yet the ChEMBL record for OXA-23 contains only two bioactivities. We asked whether any ChEMBL-recorded OXA-23 ligand binds the enzyme's active site more strongly than avibactam. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q9L4P2 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL3885669, 2 bioactivities → PubChem/RDKit similarity, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked avibactam on the 1.15 Å OXA-23 structure 4JF5, centred on the active-site citrate (4.25 Å from the catalytic Ser79 oxygen, verified). Avibactam scored −6.54 kcal/mol; the only other ChEMBL ligand, a boronate with a measured Ki of 0.74 nM, could not be docked at all — AutoDock Vina does not support the boron atom type. We therefore docked durlobactam, the diazabicyclooctane inhibitor approved in 2023 as sulbactam–durlobactam and now the IDSA-preferred CRAB therapy, on the same centre: it scored −6.42 kcal/mol, a 0.12 kcal/mol tie with avibactam, with tight pose consistency and no PAINS alerts. The honest limit: both drugs are reversible covalent inhibitors, and Vina scores only non-covalent poses — the covalent bond to Ser79 is missing from both numbers — so the tie says nothing about their real inhibitory potency, and the 0.74 nM boronate remains unscored by this method. The claim that either diazabicyclooctane is the better OXA-23 inhibitor would be refuted if a biochemical inhibition assay (k2/Ki) shows a >10-fold difference. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week enzyme-plus-MIC test of avibactam, durlobactam and a boronate inhibitor against OXA-23-producing clinical isolates.
summary: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) sits atop the WHO critical-priority list, and in most of the world its carbapenem resistance is OXA-23 — yet the ChEMBL record for OXA-23 contains only two bioactivities.

title: Three Nanomolar NLRP3 Ligands Dock at −8.4 to −8.9 kcal/mol Behind MCC950 — but None Beats It, and MCC950 Itself Failed on Liver Toxicity
abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome drives IL-1β release in gout, atherosclerosis, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, yet no NLRP3 inhibitor is approved: the benchmark, MCC950, was halted in Phase II over hepatotoxicity. We asked whether ChEMBL-recorded NLRP3 ligands bind the NACHT domain more strongly than MCC950 itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q96P20 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL1741208, 55 bioactivities → PubChem/RDKit similarity, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked the top four leads and MCC950 on the 2.7 Å NLRP3 NACHT-domain structure 8WSM, centred on the co-crystallised inhibitor (verified centroid). MCC950 scored best at −10.08 kcal/mol; the three leads scored −8.86, −8.68 and −8.35 kcal/mol, with tight pose consistency; their measured IC50 values are 3.2–3.6 nM, and none of the 26 pipeline leads carries a PAINS alert. The honest limit: every lead docks 1.2–1.7 kcal/mol worse than MCC950, the margins are inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the reference drug's failure was toxicity, not potency — so a compound that merely matches MCC950's binding inherits its problem. The claim that any of these leads is a better NLRP3 drug would be refuted if a cellular IL-1β assay shows no potency advantage over MCC950's ~7.5 nM, or if a hepatotoxicity screen shows the same liability. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week cellular-plus-toxicity test of the three leads against MCC950, with a blood–brain-barrier screen — the property the field's newer inhibitors (MCC7840/Inzomelid) were designed for.
summary: The NLRP3 inflammasome drives IL-1β release in gout, atherosclerosis, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, yet no NLRP3 inhibitor is approved: the benchmark, MCC950, was halted in Phase II over hepatotoxicity. We asked whether ChEMBL-recorded NLRP3 ligands bind the NACHT domain more strongly than MCC950 itself.

title: Two Sub-Nanomolar MDM2 Ligands Out-Dock Idasanutlin on the 1.13 Å HDM2 Structure — but the Margin Is Inside Vina Noise and the Most Potent Measured Compound Docks Worst
abstract: p53 is inactivated in most human cancers, and in tumours that keep wild-type TP53 the E3 ubiquitin ligase MDM2 is the usual silencer — yet no MDM2 inhibitor is approved anywhere: idasanutlin, the most advanced, failed its Phase 3 MIRROS overall-survival endpoint and Roche discontinued development. We asked whether ChEMBL-recorded sub-nanomolar MDM2 ligands bind the true p53-binding pocket more strongly than idasanutlin itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q00987 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL5023, 54 bioactivities → PubChem/RDKit similarity, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked the top four leads and idasanutlin on the 1.13 Å HDM2 N-terminal-domain structure 6Q9L, centred on the co-crystallised ligand (chain A centroid, verified). Two leads scored beyond re-docked idasanutlin: CHEMBL3125534 −9.52 and CHEMBL3318767 −9.30 kcal/mol versus −8.55 kcal/mol for idasanutlin, with tight pose consistency; their measured IC50 values are 0.10 and 0.096 nM, and none of the five compounds carries a PAINS alert. The honest limit: both margins (0.97 and 0.75 kcal/mol) lie inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, the most potent measured compound (CHEMBL3657031, IC50 0.05 nM) docked worst (−7.67 kcal/mol), and every compound in the set — idasanutlin included — carries Lipinski violations driven by logP 5–8. The claim that either lead is a better MDM2 inhibitor would be refuted if a fluorescence-polarisation binding assay shows a >10-fold IC50 loss against idasanutlin, or if cellular p53-stabilisation assays show no advantage. The falsifiable next step is an 8–12-week binding-plus-cellular test of the two leads against wild-type p53 cancer lines.
summary: p53 is inactivated in most human cancers, and in tumours that keep wild-type TP53 the E3 ubiquitin ligase MDM2 is the usual silencer — yet no MDM2 inhibitor is approved anywhere: idasanutlin, the most advanced, failed its Phase 3 MIRROS overall-survival endpoint and Roche discontinued development.

title: Baloxavir Acid Re-Docks at −6.62 kcal/mol on the Influenza PA Endonuclease Fragment Structure — but the ChEMBL Ligand Set Is Undockable and the Older Inhibitor L-742,001 Scores Better
abstract: Influenza causes about a billion infections a year, and baloxavir marboxil — the only approved cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitor — is losing ground to treatment-emergent PA I38T substitutions, which appear in roughly 10% of treated adults and up to about 23% of treated children. We asked whether ChEMBL-recorded inhibitors of the influenza A polymerase acidic (PA) endonuclease bind the true active site more strongly than baloxavir acid itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P15659 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL3885620, 7 bioactivities → PubChem/RDKit similarity, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we found the ChEMBL ligand set unusable: all seven recorded ligands are giant molecules (MW 1,686–2,722 Da, 52–80 rotatable bonds) that failed conformer generation, so none could be docked. Instead we re-docked baloxavir acid on the 2.2 Å PA endonuclease fragment structure 5IEQ, centred on the co-crystallised fragment (verified centroid), and compared it with two literature compounds docked on the same centre: the diketo-acid inhibitor L-742,001 scored −7.17 kcal/mol and the co-crystallised fragment EBSI-747 scored −5.55 kcal/mol, against −6.62 kcal/mol for baloxavir acid, all with tight pose consistency and no PAINS alerts. The honest limit: the 0.55 kcal/mol gap between L-742,001 and baloxavir acid lies inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, baloxavir acid is roughly 100-fold more potent than L-742,001 by measured enzyme IC50 (low-nanomolar versus 0.5 µM), and the 5IEQ structure contains no catalytic metal ions — yet both inhibitors bind by chelating the two active-site metals, so the scoring omits the interaction that matters most. The claim that L-742,001 is the better PA inhibitor would be refuted if a metal-containing endonuclease assay shows baloxavir acid retaining its ~100-fold potency advantage. The falsifiable next step is a 8–12-week metal-containing enzyme-plus-cellular test of baloxavir acid against L-742,001 and its analogues on wild-type and I38T PA.
summary: Influenza causes about a billion infections a year, and baloxavir marboxil — the only approved cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitor — is losing ground to treatment-emergent PA I38T substitutions, which appear in roughly 10% of treated adults and up to about 23% of treated children.

title: No Structure to Dock On: Five Single-Digit-Nanomolar TbNMT Inhibitors Share One Scaffold, and the Blood–Brain Barrier — Not Potency — Decides Whether Any of Them Treats Stage-2 Sleeping Sickness
abstract: Human African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness) is down to 471 reported cases worldwide in 2025, and the WHO target is interruption of transmission by 2030 — but the last cases are the hardest, and they need drugs that reach the brain. DDD85646, a pyrazole-sulfonamide inhibitor of Trypanosoma brucei N-myristoyltransferase (TbNMT), is potent (enzyme IC50 1–2 nM) and cures stage-1 (haemolymphatic) infection in rodents, yet poor central nervous system exposure restricts it to stage 1. We asked whether ChEMBL holds a DDD85646 analogue that keeps the potency and fixes the brain exposure. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q388H8 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL3988596, 60 bioactivities → PubChem/RDKit similarity, PAINS and ADMET screen), we retrieved five single-digit-nanomolar TbNMT inhibitors, including DDD85646 itself. Docking was not performed: no Trypanosoma brucei NMT crystal structure exists in the PDB (verified 2026-11-18; the only NMT structures are from Leishmania major and Aspergillus fumigatus), and docking a T. brucei inhibitor onto another species' enzyme would be a false result. The honest finding is structural, not numerical: all five compounds share one scaffold (identical TPSA 92.15 Å², the published pyrazole-sulfonamide core), so none obviously escapes the parent's brain-exposure problem on descriptors alone — the smallest and least lipophilic analogue, CHEMBL4112331 (MW 426.55, logP 2.31), is the only one inside all standard CNS descriptor bands, and even it sits at TPSA 92.15 Å², just above the usual <90 Å² blood–brain-barrier guideline. The claim that any analogue is a stage-2 candidate would be refuted if PAMPA-BBB or MDCK-MDR1 testing shows no analogue beats DDD85646's brain exposure. The falsifiable next step is a 4-week BBB-permeability screen of the four analogues, not another potency assay.
summary: Human African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness) is down to 471 reported cases worldwide in 2025, and the WHO target is interruption of transmission by 2030 — but the last cases are the hardest, and they need drugs that reach the brain.

title: A Target With No Approved Drug: Four PanC Inhibitors Dock at −10.64 to −7.66 kcal/mol on the 1.5 Å Fragment Structure — but the 90 nM Inhibitor Was Never Docked, and the Reference Drug Could Not Be Docked at All
abstract: Pantothenate synthetase (PanC) is essential for Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in vitro and survival in mice, is absent from mammals, and has no approved drug — the ideal profile of an unexploited target, and the reason it has attracted twenty years of inhibitor chemistry without a clinical candidate. We asked what the ChEMBL record actually contains for this target and whether its inhibitors bind the known inhibitor pocket. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P9WIL5 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL6069, 59 bioactivities → PubChem/RDKit similarity, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked four leads on the 1.5 Å PanC structure 3IUB, centred on its co-crystallised fragment-derived inhibitor. The four leads scored −10.64 to −7.66 kcal/mol with tight pose consistency, and their measured potencies are 1.0–2.0 µM. The honest limits are twofold and both matter more than the scores. First, the reference compound, actinomycin D — the only named, PubChem-resolvable literature PanC inhibitor (IC50 22.44 µM) — could not be docked at all: Vina hit its 30-minute timeout on a 1,255 Da, highly flexible ligand, so there is no re-docked reference benchmark in this paper. Second, the similarity anchor (actinomycin D) biased lead selection so strongly that the most potent ChEMBL PanC inhibitor, CHEMBL428787 (IC50 90 nM), ranked 17th and was never docked, while the best-docked compound (CHEMBL2435654, −10.64 kcal/mol) has a measured Kd of only 1.8 µM. The claim that any docked compound here is a PanC lead would be refuted if a direct enzyme assay shows no inhibition below 10 µM, or if re-docking the 90 nM compound scores worse than the compounds reported here. The falsifiable next step is a 4-week enzyme assay plus a re-dock of the five most potent ChEMBL PanC inhibitors — selected by potency, not by similarity to actinomycin D.
summary: Pantothenate synthetase (PanC) is essential for Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in vitro and survival in mice, is absent from mammals, and has no approved drug — the ideal profile of an unexploited target, and the reason it has attracted twenty years of inhibitor chemistry without a clinical candidate.

title: Posaconazole and Itraconazole Dock Best on the Naegleria CYP51 Structure — and the Ranking Matches the Published Potencies — but Karachi's Brain-Eating Amoeba Kills in Days, and No Azole Has a Measured Brain Exposure in PAM
abstract: Primary amoebic meningoencephalitis (PAM), caused by Naegleria fowleri, kills more than 97% of patients within five to seven days of symptom onset, and Karachi — where infection now comes through ablution with tap water, not swimming — reports more cases than the United States recorded in fifty years. The parasite's sterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51) is an essential, structurally characterised target, and the published conazole potencies span three orders of magnitude (itraconazole and posaconazole EC50 0.01 µM; fluconazole 13.9 µM). We asked whether docking on the Naegleria CYP51–posaconazole structure reproduces that ranking. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB A0A2H4A2U9 → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked posaconazole on its own co-crystal structure 5TL8 (1.71 Å) at −10.91 kcal/mol (reproducing the pipeline's −10.84 within 0.07), then docked the other four published conazoles at the same centroid. The ranking matches the published potencies: itraconazole −11.59, posaconazole −10.91, ketoconazole −10.21, isavuconazole −8.96, fluconazole −7.01 kcal/mol (Spearman rho 0.95, n = 5, tied ranks). The honest limits: the pipeline's own ChEMBL ligand retrieval failed for this target — no ChEMBL target exists for N. fowleri CYP51, so it silently substituted human maltase-glucoamylase (CHEMBL2074) and returned alpha-glucosidase inhibitors as "leads"; those scores are discarded, not reported. Three of the five conazoles carry RDKit PAINS alerts despite being approved drugs, which says more about the filter than about the drugs. And no azole has a measured brain exposure in PAM — the property that decides whether any of this matters, since PAM is a brain infection. The claim that itraconazole or posaconazole is the best PAM candidate would be refuted if brain-exposure measurement shows it does not reach the brain, or if a mouse PAM model shows no survival benefit. The falsifiable next step is a 4-week brain-exposure and mouse-PAM efficacy test of posaconazole versus itraconazole, not another docking run.
summary: Primary amoebic meningoencephalitis (PAM), caused by Naegleria fowleri, kills more than 97% of patients within five to seven days of symptom onset, and Karachi — where infection now comes through ablution with tap water, not swimming — reports more cases than the United States recorded in fifty years.

title: Four Nanomolar Gyrase Inhibitors Out-Score Moxifloxacin at the M. tuberculosis Cleavage Site — but the Margin Is Inside Vina Noise and the D94G Test Is Still Missing
abstract: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) kills because fluoroquinolones fail: resistance is dominated by gyrA mutations D94G and A90V in the quinolone resistance-determining region, and moxifloxacin — a core drug of the WHO BPaLM regimen — loses activity against them. We asked whether ChEMBL-recorded nanomolar inhibitors of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA gyrase A/B complex bind the true fluoroquinolone cleavage site more strongly than moxifloxacin itself. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P9WG45 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL3430898, 46 bioactivities → PubChem/RDKit similarity, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we re-docked the top four leads and moxifloxacin on the moxifloxacin-bound cleavage complex 5BS8 (2.4 Å), centred on the co-crystallised moxifloxacin. The four leads scored −10.87 to −10.37 kcal/mol versus −9.38 kcal/mol for re-docked moxifloxacin, with tight pose consistency (top-3 spread ≤0.6 kcal/mol); their measured enzyme IC50 values are 5, 10, 65 and 780 nM, and none carries a PAINS alert. The honest limit: every margin over moxifloxacin (0.99–1.49 kcal/mol) lies inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, so docking alone cannot rank these compounds, and none has yet been tested against a D94G or A90V mutant enzyme or whole cells. The claim that any of these four is a better fluoroquinolone-alternative would be refuted if re-docking on a D94G cleavage complex, or a mutant-enzyme assay, shows a ≥2 kcal/mol or >10-fold IC50 loss. The falsifiable next step is a 8–12-week enzyme-plus-MIC test of the four leads against wild-type and D94G/A90V M. tuberculosis gyrase and clinical isolates.
summary: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) kills because fluoroquinolones fail: resistance is dominated by gyrA mutations D94G and A90V in the quinolone resistance-determining region, and moxifloxacin — a core drug of the WHO BPaLM regimen — loses activity against them.

title: Sub-Nanomolar FXR Agonists Out-Dock Obeticholic Acid on the CDCA-Bound FXR Structure — but All Four Are Lipinski Failures and the Pruritus–LDL Trade-Off Is a Class Problem, Not a Potency Problem
abstract: Obeticholic acid (OCA), the first farnesoid X receptor (FXR) agonist, improved liver histology in MASH but failed regulatory approval for the indication: its antifibrotic benefit travels with dose-dependent pruritus (23% vs 6% on placebo in FLINT; up to 51% at higher doses) and a pro-atherogenic lipid shift (higher LDL cholesterol, lower HDL), and its United States NASH programme ended with a Complete Response Letter in 2023. We asked whether more potent FXR agonists solve this problem. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q96RI1 → ChEMBL target CHEMBL2047, 57 bioactivities → PubChem/RDKit similarity, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked the top four leads and OCA on the FXR ligand-binding domain structure 6HL1 (1.6 Å, chenodeoxycholic acid bound), centred on the co-crystallised bile acid. The four leads scored −10.42 to −8.88 kcal/mol versus −8.39 kcal/mol for re-docked OCA, and their measured potencies are sub-nanomolar (EC50 0.1, 0.1 and 0.251 nM; IC50 0.09 nM). The honest limit: all four are highly lipophilic (logP 6.2–8.4), three carry two Lipinski violations and molecular weights above 600 Da, one lead's pose set includes a +8.90 kcal/mol non-binding mode, and docking cannot measure partial agonism, pruritus or LDL effects at all — the liabilities that actually killed OCA. The claim that greater FXR potency means a better MASH drug would be refuted if these leads show full-agonist suppression of CYP7A1 per unit of antifibrotic signal, or pruritus/LDL signals in the same range as OCA in a relevant model. The falsifiable next step is a partial-agonism assay (co-regulator recruitment plus CYP7A1 suppression) and a lipid/pruritus read-out for the two least lipophilic leads, not another affinity screen.

title: Import Failure Before Leak: The Blood–Brain Barrier as a Supply Line Whose Early Shutdown Initiates Alzheimer's Disease — a Falsifiable Model and a Re-Ranking of Brain-Delivery Strategies
abstract: For a century the blood–brain barrier (BBB) has been treated as a fortress whose failure in Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a leak: tight junctions break, albumin and fibrinogen flood in, neuroinflammation follows. A study published in Cell on 11 November 2026 (Zhou et al.) overturns the order of events. Using bioorthogonal proteomics, the authors tracked 861 plasma proteins in mice and found the healthy BBB samples 191 and permits only 92 (10.7%) into the brain parenchyma — a selective import system, not a wall. The imported proteins home to specific cell types: liver-derived apolipoprotein A1 (APOA1) crosses via SR-B1 and engages astrocytic ABCA1, an Alzheimer's risk gene, driving cholesterol efflux that supports synapse integrity; alpha-1 antitrypsin (SERPINA1) homes to microglia. In early-stage 5xFAD mice, the barrier first remodels transport — APOA1 uptake falls, SERPINA1 uptake rises — before any leak; hepatic overexpression of APOA1 restores brain APOA1 and rescues astrocytic, synaptic and behavioural deficits. We add two new quantitative facts and a synthesis. First, from UniProt (P02647), human APOA1 is a 267-amino-acid, 30,778 Da protein — 68 times the 450 Da passive-diffusion cut-off — so its brain entry is necessarily receptor-mediated, and any drug strategy that relies on passive entry cannot reproduce it. Second, the human observational record is consistent with, but does not prove, the import-first model: in the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort (n = 429 non-demented elderly, mean follow-up 2.5 years), lower plasma APOA1 predicted clinical progression in APOE ε4 carriers with subjective cognitive decline (hazard ratio 5.0; 95% CI 1.3–18.9), while higher cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) APOA1 predicted progression overall (HR 1.3 per standard deviation; 95% CI 1.0–1.6) — a pattern compatible with a disrupted plasma-to-brain gradient, but equally compatible with leak. Falsifiable claim: in preclinical AD, BBB import of liver-derived APOA1 falls before measurable barrier leak, and the CSF:plasma APOA1 ratio predicts clinical progression earlier than amyloid-PET positivity. Falsifier: a longitudinal human cohort in which the CSF:plasma APOA1 ratio does not fall before amyloid positivity, or in which gadolinium-measured leak precedes the import fall, refutes the import-first ordering; and a liver-targeted APOA1 intervention that raises brain APOA1 without slowing tau spread refutes the disease-modifying version of the claim while leaving the biomarker version intact. Causal identification for the human claim is association only; causality is established in mice only. We re-rank brain-delivery strategies against this model: receptor-mediated import restoration (endogenous SR-B1/APOA1 route; transferrin-receptor shuttles, with a company-reported >65-fold delivery gain in preclinical studies) outranks leak-sealing and passive-diffusion strategies, and we show why the peptide drugs that failed in Parkinson's trials could never have tested their own mechanism. Policy implication: Pakistan's health research funders should add the plasma/CSF APOA1 ratio to the national dementia cohort protocol and fund a liver-targeted APOA1 pilot before funding another leak-sealing trial — under the Islamic principle of hifz al-nafs (preservation of life), one of the five objectives of the Shariah.
summary: For a century the blood–brain barrier (BBB) has been treated as a fortress whose failure in Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a leak: tight junctions break, albumin and fibrinogen flood in, neuroinflammation follows. A study published in Cell on 11 November 2026 (Zhou et al.) overturns the order of events.

title: Riociguat Re-Docks at −9.96 kcal/mol on the Cryo-EM sGC Structure 7D9R, but Two 3 nM Stimulators Score 2.38 kcal/mol Apart
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension affects about 1% of the global population, and its treatment rests on the NO–sGC–cGMP pathway: riociguat, the first soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, sensitises the enzyme to nitric oxide and stimulates it directly, and improved the 6-minute walk distance by 36 m in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PATENT-1) and 46 m in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CHEST-1). We asked whether the standard rigid-docking benchmark of this series can rank sGC stimulators at all, using the riociguat-bound cryo-EM structure 7D9R (3.7 Å) after the pipeline's first run failed on the wrong domain — the ligand-free catalytic structure 4NI2. Riociguat re-docked into its own H-NOX pocket at −9.96 kcal/mol with three poses within 0.06 kcal/mol, and the five most potent ChEMBL leads (cellular EC50 1–4 nM) scored from −10.97 to −8.59. The rank correlation against measured potency was Spearman rho −0.41 (n = 5, standard convention), a moderate correct-direction correlation that does not reach the pre-stated refutation threshold of −0.5 — and the table itself shows why: the two compounds with the identical measured EC50 of 3 nM score 2.38 kcal/mol apart, the best and the worst of the five. Falsifiable claim: rigid Vina docking on a single cryo-EM structure cannot rank sGC stimulators whose potencies span less than its own noise. Falsifier: a rescoring method, or a second structure, that reaches rho −0.5 or below against the same five EC50s, or a head-to-head cellular assay that reproduces the docking order. The screen's value is the calibration, not the table: the next sGC stimulator should be judged by a cellular assay, not by a docking score.
summary: Pulmonary hypertension affects about 1% of the global population, and its treatment rests on the NO–sGC–cGMP pathway: riociguat, the first soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, sensitises the enzyme to nitric oxide and stimulates it directly, and improved the 6-minute walk distance by 36 m in pulmonary arterial hyperte…

title: Presatovir Scores −6.15 kcal/mol on Prefusion RSV F (5KWW), but Rigid Docking Cannot Rank RSV Fusion Inhibitors
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) caused an estimated 33.0 million lower-respiratory episodes and 101,400 deaths in children under five in 2019, with more than 97 percent of deaths in low- and middle-income countries, and no small-molecule antiviral is approved. Presatovir, an RSV fusion inhibitor, cut viral load in a human challenge study but failed its Phase 2b trial in haematopoietic-cell transplant recipients, with no viral-load or clinical benefit and treatment-emergent fusion-protein substitutions in 21 percent of treated patients with lower-respiratory infection. We asked whether standard rigid docking can rank RSV fusion inhibitors at all. A first automated run docked onto the wrong structure — a 51-residue fragment (29QJ) — and was discarded in full. The corrected benchmark docks presatovir, the co-crystallised inhibitor rilematovir, and five ChEMBL leads with measured potency onto the prefusion F structure 5KWW (2.5 angstrom), at the verified rilematovir-pocket centre. Presatovir scores −6.15 kcal/mol and rilematovir −5.36, but the ranking against measured potency is essentially random (Spearman rho +0.1, n = 5): the most potent measured compound (EC50 0.47 nM) scores −4.94, while presatovir's own ChEMBL record scores best at −6.53, and the same molecule docked twice from two SMILES encodings differs by 0.38 kcal/mol. Rigid Vina docking on a single prefusion structure cannot rank RSV fusion inhibitors, and no lead can be claimed better than presatovir from this screen. The falsifier is a rescoring method, or a second prefusion structure, that reaches rho of −0.5 or below against the same five measured potencies, or a cell assay that reproduces the docking order.
summary: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) caused an estimated 33.0 million lower-respiratory episodes and 101,400 deaths in children under five in 2019, with more than 97 percent of deaths in low- and middle-income countries, and no small-molecule antiviral is approved.

title: Rigid Docking Cannot Rank the GRL0617 Series on SARS-CoV-2 PLpro: the 2.67 µM Reference Scores Best and the 42 µM Compound Beats Both Leads
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) cleaves the viral polyprotein and strips ubiquitin and ISG15 from host proteins, suppressing type-I interferon — a second viral protease with no approved inhibitor, unlike the main protease (Mpro), which has nirmatrelvir. GRL0617, a non-covalent PLpro inhibitor first described against SARS-CoV in 2008, remains the best-validated PLpro chemotype: it inhibits SARS-CoV-2 PLpro at 2.05 micromolar (median of 21 ChEMBL records) and blocks viral replication in cells and in mouse models, and its optimised analogues reach 0.11–0.67 micromolar. We benchmarked rigid AutoDock Vina docking on the GRL0617-bound structure 7JRN (2.48 angstrom) against five compounds from a single FRET assay (Ma et al. 2021): GRL0617 (2.67 micromolar in this assay) plus four analogues spanning 0.11–42 micromolar. The re-dock control worked — GRL0617 scored −9.90 kcal/mol in its own pocket — but the ranking failed: Spearman rho = +0.15 (n = 5). The weakest compound (42 micromolar) scored third-best (−9.14), beating both named leads Jun9-72-2 (−7.74) and Jun9-84-3 (−8.21), while the most potent analogue (0.11 micromolar) scored second (−9.74). All five compounds are PAINS-clean, so the failure is not assay artefacts but the method: the analogues' advantage is an ionic hydrogen bond to Asp164 and closure of the flexible BL2 loop, which rigid docking cannot score. Falsifiable claim: rigid Vina docking into 7JRN cannot rank PLpro inhibitors, and any PLpro claim resting on it alone is untested. The falsifier is a head-to-head test — run induced-fit docking or MM-GBSA on the same five compounds in the same pocket: if it recovers rho below −0.5 where rigid Vina gives +0.15, the failure is the rigidity and the claim stands; if it also fails, the pocket itself defeats scoring-based ranking.
summary: SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) cleaves the viral polyprotein and strips ubiquitin and ISG15 from host proteins, suppressing type-I interferon — a second viral protease with no approved inhibitor, unlike the main protease (Mpro), which has nirmatrelvir.

title: No Structure to Dock On: MMV390048 and the Plasmodium PI4K Target That ChEMBL and the PDB Do Not Contain
abstract: Malaria still killed an estimated 597,000 people in 2023, from 263 million cases (WHO World Malaria Report 2024), and artemisinin partial resistance makes a new mechanism a priority. Plasmodium falciparum phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase (PfPI4K) is the target of MMV390048, the first PI4K inhibitor to reach clinical development: it clears blood-stage parasites at 28 nM in vitro, blocks liver stages and gametocytes, and cured 8 of 8 P. vivax patients at day 14 on a single 120 mg dose, before its Phase 2a trial was stopped over emerging teratogenicity data. We asked whether the standard computational benchmark used in this series, ChEMBL potency retrieval plus AutoDock Vina docking, can evaluate this target at all. It cannot, and the failure is structural, not technical: ChEMBL holds no target carrying the PfPI4K accession Q8I406, and no experimental structure of PfPI4K exists in the PDB, so docking was skipped rather than faked. A first pipeline run that ignored this returned 26 human maltase inhibitors as PfPI4K leads and was discarded. What could be computed honestly was computed: MMV390048 is drug-like (MW 393.39, logP 3.82, zero Lipinski violations, PAINS-clean) with a weak ToxGuard read-across (max similarity 0.382); four close 2D analogues (Tanimoto 0.72–0.79) are likewise clean but have no published PfPI4K activity. Falsifiable claim: the 2-aminopyridine scaffold's future depends on an enzyme assay, not more docking. If none of the four analogues inhibits PfPI4K below 1 micromolar, the similarity neighbourhood is a dead end; if one does, it is the backup series that MMV390048's termination left behind. The falsifier is a single PfPI4K enzyme assay, which no Pakistani laboratory currently runs.
summary: Malaria still killed an estimated 597,000 people in 2023, from 263 million cases (WHO World Malaria Report 2024), and artemisinin partial resistance makes a new mechanism a priority.

title: Rigid Docking Gets the Dicarboxylates Right on IMP-1 but Collapses Four Captopril Stereoisomers into 0.08 kcal/mol for a 60-Fold Potency Range
abstract: IMP-1 is a subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) that hydrolyses almost all β-lactams, including carbapenems, and no clinically approved inhibitor exists for it. We benchmarked rigid AutoDock Vina docking (v1.2.7) against measured IMP-1 inhibition for six compounds spanning 240 nM to 436 µM: the dicarboxylates 3AP-DPA (IC50 240 nM) and dipicolinic acid (3,030 nM), and the four captopril stereoisomers (d 7.2, l 23.3, epi-d 173.2, epi-l 436 µM), docked into the d-captopril-bound structure 4C1G (1.71 Å) and replicated on 6JED (1.57 Å). Falsifiable claim: Vina ranks the dicarboxylates ahead of the thiols and orders 3AP-DPA ahead of dipicolinic acid, but cannot rank the four captopril stereoisomers. Falsifier: a metal-aware re-dock (Zn(II) retained, metal-coordination term) that orders the four stereoisomers in measured order with a spread ≥1 kcal/mol refutes the blindness claim. On 4C1G, 3AP-DPA scored best (−7.42 kcal/mol) and dipicolinic acid second (−6.50), a 0.92 kcal/mol gap for a 12.6-fold measured difference (1.50 kcal/mol), and the overall rank correlation was Spearman ρ = −0.66 (n = 6, correct direction). But the four stereoisomers collapsed into 0.08 kcal/mol (−5.90 to −5.98) for a 60-fold measured range (2.43 kcal/mol), with the weakest, epi-l-captopril, scoring joint-best; within the series ρ = +0.20. The 6JED replication reproduced the pattern exactly (ρ = −0.66; stereoisomer spread 0.34 kcal/mol; epi-l again best of the four). The mechanism is stated in advance: the pipeline's receptor preparation strips the two catalytic Zn(II) ions, and Vina has no metal-coordination term, so inhibitors whose binding is Zn chelation are scored on shape alone — and four stereoisomers have the same shape. Rigid metal-free docking can shortlist dicarboxylate scaffolds for IMP-1; it cannot rank thiol stereoisomers, and any IMP-1 screen that uses it without a metal-aware step will mis-prioritise. Keywords: IMP-1; metallo-β-lactamase; captopril; stereoisomers; dipicolinic acid; 3AP-DPA; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; carbapenem resistance; Pakistan
summary: IMP-1 is a subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) that hydrolyses almost all β-lactams, including carbapenems, and no clinically approved inhibitor exists for it.

title: Pemigatinib Re-Docks at −8.83 kcal/mol on FGFR2 2PVF, but the Most Potent Measured Inhibitor Scores Worst and the Most Potent Lead Was Never Docked
abstract: FGFR2 fusions drive 10–15% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and pemigatinib, the first approved FGFR inhibitor for this disease, produced a 35.5% objective response rate in FIGHT-202. We benchmarked rigid AutoDock Vina docking (v1.2.7) against measured FGFR2 inhibition for four sub-nanomolar compounds on the activated FGFR2 kinase structure 2PVF (1.8 Å), with the grid centre audited to exactly 0.00 Å from the ATP-analogue centroid. Pemigatinib re-docked at −8.83 kcal/mol, reproduced to −8.90 by its own ChEMBL record, a 0.07 kcal/mol duplicate. But the ranking fails: the most potent measured inhibitor, CHEMBL4870179 (IC50 0.15 nM), scored worst at −8.01, and the most potent compound in the whole 26-lead set (CHEMBL5173892, 0.11 nM) was never docked, because the pipeline's similarity-dominated ranking placed it 20th. Spearman rho is +0.40 (n = 4). ChEMBL mutant records add the clinically decisive number: pemigatinib loses about 6,000-fold potency against the gatekeeper mutant FGFR2 V564F (IC50 1,460.5 nM), a loss no wild-type docking score can see. The honest limit cuts deeper than the ranking: the two leads' sub-nanomolar values come from a single document, while a patent document reports 100 nM for both. Falsifiable claim: rigid docking on the activated FGFR2 structure cannot rank sub-nanomolar FGFR2 inhibitors. A re-dock on an inhibitor-bound, inactive-conformation FGFR2 structure that recovers the measured order with rho at or below −0.5 would refute it; so would a prospective enzyme assay showing CHEMBL5171314, the best-docked compound, underperforming pemigatinib in cells.
summary: FGFR2 fusions drive 10–15% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and pemigatinib, the first approved FGFR inhibitor for this disease, produced a 35.5% objective response rate in FIGHT-202.

title: The Ten-Percent Ceiling: Ibn Khaldun's Fiscal Curve and Pakistan's Tax Record, 2001–2025
abstract: Question. Pakistan has raised its statutory tax rates repeatedly for a quarter of a century — general sales tax from 16% to 18%, a new super tax up to 10%, a 29% corporate rate stacked with surcharges — yet its tax-to-GDP ratio has not durably risen. Is the country on the wrong side of the fiscal curve Ibn Khaldun described in 1377, where higher rates shrink the base faster than they raise the yield? Claim. Yes — on the evidence available, Pakistan sits past the peak of its Khaldunian curve. Over 2001–2024 the tax-to-GDP ratio moved only inside a 7.9–11.4% band (mean 9.7%), and the Federal Board of Revenue's own ratio stayed in single digits for 24 consecutive fiscal years (2000-01 to 2023-24), while statutory rates rose at every margin. The binding constraint is the base, not the rate: about 5.9 million returns were filed for tax year 2025 in a country of 241.5 million people, and only about 3 million taxpayers show any taxable income at all. Falsifier. The claim is refuted if either (i) the FBR-only tax-to-GDP ratio rises above 12% and holds there for three consecutive fiscal years with no new statutory rate increase, or (ii) a legislated cut in a major rate — general sales tax back to 16%, or super-tax relief — is followed within two fiscal years by a fall, rather than a rise, in the FBR tax-to-GDP ratio. The fiscal year 2025-26 outturn (target Rs 14.131 trillion) is the first scheduled test. Identification. Association only. This is a descriptive time-series test on published aggregates, with no control group and no randomised or quasi-experimental variation in rates. Confounders — GDP growth, inflation, IMF programme conditions, enforcement drives — are named, not controlled. The paper falsifies the claim that "rate rises raise the ratio"; it does not estimate a causal effect of any single rate. A regression-discontinuity design on the February 2023 GST rise (17% → 18%) and a randomised rate pilot are proposed as the causal tests. One clean number: 24 years below 10% — the number of consecutive fiscal years the FBR's tax-to-GDP ratio stayed in single digits while rates rose. The stakes number is 3 million: the people in a country of 241.5 million who show any taxable income. Keywords: Ibn Khaldun; Laffer curve; tax-to-GDP ratio; Pakistan; FBR; fiscal policy; tax base; super tax; maqasid; 'adl.
summary: Question. Pakistan has raised its statutory tax rates repeatedly for a quarter of a century — general sales tax from 16% to 18%, a new super tax up to 10%, a 29% corporate rate stacked with surcharges — yet its tax-to-GDP ratio has not durably risen.

title: Dapagliflozin Re-Docks at −11.00 kcal/mol on Its Own Cryo-EM Structure — but the Screen Ranks the Most Potent Lead Last
abstract: Dapagliflozin blocks the kidney's sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) and has transformed diabetic kidney disease and heart failure, but finding a better SGLT2 inhibitor still relies on screens that must first prove they can rank the drugs we already have. We asked whether a standard automated docking pipeline ranks SGLT2 inhibitors by their measured potency. The pipeline (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → Vina 1.2.7) found no X-ray structure for SGLT2 and skipped docking entirely, so we docked dapagliflozin, four ChEMBL leads and empagliflozin on 8HEZ, the 2.8 angstrom cryo-EM structure of human SGLT2 bound to dapagliflozin itself, with the grid centre verified as the bound dapagliflozin's centroid. Dapagliflozin re-docks at −11.00 kcal/mol; its duplicate ChEMBL record scores −11.61, a 0.61 kcal/mol gap between identical molecules that sets the run's noise floor. The lead CHEMBL3703792 leads at −12.34, empagliflozin scores −12.03, and the LeadForge star lead CHEMBL5288495 scores −11.48 — but the docking rank against the measured potencies is exactly inverted (Spearman rho −1.0, n = 4): the most potent lead (IC50 0.308 nM) scores worst (−9.76) and the least potent (0.551 nM) scores best. The measured band is only 1.8-fold wide, so the inversion is a property of a band too narrow to rank, not a real anti-correlation — and empagliflozin, six times less potent than dapagliflozin (3.1 versus 0.49 nM), still out-scores it by 1.03 kcal/mol. The screen cannot rank SGLT2 inhibitors within this potency band, and the star lead is indistinguishable from dapagliflozin itself (0.48 kcal/mol behind its duplicate record, inside the 0.61 noise floor). The falsifiable next step is a glucose-uptake assay: if the measured IC50 rank does not match the docking rank, docking is not a ranking tool for this target. And the polyol-escape caveat from Paper #3 stands: an SGLT2-only inhibitor, however potent, does not address the sorbitol pathway that damages retina, kidney and nerve.
summary: Dapagliflozin blocks the kidney's sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) and has transformed diabetic kidney disease and heart failure, but finding a better SGLT2 inhibitor still relies on screens that must first prove they can rank the drugs we already have.

title: Olaparib Re-Docks at −11.24 kcal/mol on PARP1, but Rigid Docking Ranks Rucaparib Last and Cannot Reproduce the PARP-Trapping Order
abstract: PARP inhibitors kill BRCA-deficient cancers by synthetic lethality, but their cytotoxicity tracks PARP trapping — the stabilisation of PARP1 on DNA — more closely than catalytic inhibition, and trapping potency varies enormously between approved drugs (talazoparib ≫ niraparib > olaparib = rucaparib ≫ veliparib) while catalytic IC50 values cluster in the low-nanomolar range. We asked whether a standard rigid-docking screen can see trapping. Using the LeadForge protocol (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → Vina 1.2.7), we docked five ChEMBL PARP1 leads and olaparib on 6NRH, the 1.50 angstrom PARP1 catalytic-domain structure, then docked the five approved inhibitors plus the PARP1-selective saruparib on the same structure and grid. Olaparib re-docks at −11.24 kcal/mol; the best ChEMBL lead, CHEMBL4845834, scores −11.85, and every docked compound is PAINS-clean. Two controls expose the screen's limits. First, the pipeline docked olaparib twice — once as the PubChem query and once as its ChEMBL record — and the same molecule scored −11.24 and −10.87, a 0.37 kcal/mol reproducibility gap that sets this run's noise floor. Second, the docking rank inverts the measured potency rank of the four ChEMBL compounds (Spearman rho −0.6), and against the published trapping order the rank correlation is only 0.43: rucaparib, a mid-tier trapper equal to olaparib, docks worst at −7.87, below veliparib, the weakest trapper. Rigid docking ranks catalytic-site fit; it cannot see trapping, and on PARP1 it cannot even rank catalytic potency within a sub-nanomolar band. The falsifiable next step is a paired enzymatic-plus-trapping assay of the same set: if the trapping order predicts cell killing and the docking order does not, screening programmes must stop ranking PARP inhibitors by docking alone.
summary: PARP inhibitors kill BRCA-deficient cancers by synthetic lethality, but their cytotoxicity tracks PARP trapping — the stabilisation of PARP1 on DNA — more closely than catalytic inhibition, and trapping potency varies enormously between approved drugs (talazoparib ≫ niraparib > olaparib = rucaparib ≫ veliparib) while c…

title: Finerenone Scores −3.41 kcal/mol on the Pipeline's 1.1 Å MR Structure but −6.83 on a 3.0 Å One — and Eplerenone Out-Scores It on Both
abstract: Finerenone, spironolactone and eplerenone all block the same mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) pocket, but their chemistry and their clinical profiles differ: finerenone is non-steroidal and highly MR-selective, spironolactone is steroidal and hormonally promiscuous, eplerenone is steroidal but selective and 36-fold weaker than finerenone at the receptor. We asked whether a standard automated docking pipeline ranks these drugs by their measured MR potencies. Using the LeadForge protocol (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → Vina 1.2.7), we docked finerenone and four ChEMBL leads on the pipeline's auto-picked structure, 4PF3 (1.1 angstrom, MR bound to the non-steroidal antagonist compound 37a), then docked the two steroidal MRAs on the same structure and re-docked three compounds on 6L88 (3.0 angstrom, MR bound to the non-steroidal antagonist esaxerenone). On 4PF3, finerenone scores −3.41 kcal/mol — worst but one — while spironolactone scores −10.16, and every compound's three poses span 5–12 kcal/mol, so the best-pose numbers are single-pose artefacts, not converged results. On 6L88 the poses converge tightly (spans 0.71–1.40 kcal/mol) and finerenone improves to −6.83, but the rank is still wrong: eplerenone (IC50 990 nM) out-scores finerenone (27.9 nM) by 1.35 kcal/mol, while spironolactone (24.2 nM) and finerenone (27.9 nM) — near-equipotent — sit 6.75 kcal/mol apart on 4PF3 and 0.92 apart on 6L88. The screen fails on both structures, for different reasons: 4PF3 fails on convergence, 6L88 converges but mis-ranks. The highest-resolution structure was the worst docking structure, and the pipeline's sub-3.0-angstrom filter excluded the better one. The falsifiable next step is a reporter-gene assay: if the measured MR IC50 rank does not match the 6L88 docking rank, docking is not a ranking tool for this target, and the lead that does top both structures (CHEMBL1215196, IC50 2.0 nM) still needs its selectivity and potassium data before it is anything more than a score.
summary: Finerenone, spironolactone and eplerenone all block the same mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) pocket, but their chemistry and their clinical profiles differ: finerenone is non-steroidal and highly MR-selective, spironolactone is steroidal and hormonally promiscuous, eplerenone is steroidal but selective and 36-fold weak…

title: Ivosidenib Scores −8.25 kcal/mol on Wild-Type IDH1 but −9.35 on the R132H Mutant — and the Pipeline Picked the Wild Type
abstract: Ivosidenib treats IDH1-mutant cancer by inhibiting the mutant enzyme (R132H) while sparing the wild type — two proteins that differ by a single amino acid — and its selectivity comes from trapping the mutant in an inactive conformation, not from binding a different pocket. We asked whether a standard automated docking pipeline ranks IDH1 inhibitors correctly. Using the LeadForge protocol (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → Vina 1.2.7), we docked ivosidenib and four ChEMBL leads on the pipeline's auto-picked structure, 6BKX — which turns out to be wild-type IDH1, not the mutant — and then re-docked the same compounds on 8T7O, the R132H mutant bound to ivosidenib itself. Ivosidenib scores −8.25 kcal/mol on the wild type and −9.35 on the mutant; every compound scores 1.10–2.20 kcal/mol stronger on the mutant, and the two structures' rankings correlate only 0.5, with the winner changing (CHEMBL4278793 on the wild type, CHEMBL4282663 on the mutant) and ivosidenib falling from second to fourth. Against the measured potencies, the wild-type ranking correlates at 0.5 and the mutant ranking at 0.1 — but the measured values span only 1–3 nM, a 3-fold band no screen can resolve, and they are the wild-type target's bioactivities, so the mutant structure is being judged against the wrong protein's numbers. The pipeline docked a mutant-selective drug on the wild-type protein and reported the scores without flagging it. The falsifiable next step is a paired mutant-versus-wild-type enzymatic assay: if the mutant-structure rank predicts the mutant IC50 rank and the wild-type rank does not, docking must be run on the mutant structure, with the variant stated in every table.
summary: Ivosidenib treats IDH1-mutant cancer by inhibiting the mutant enzyme (R132H) while sparing the wild type — two proteins that differ by a single amino acid — and its selectivity comes from trapping the mutant in an inactive conformation, not from binding a different pocket.

title: Orforglipron Re-Docks at −10.8 kcal/mol in Its Own GLP-1R Pocket but Only −7.66 on the Pipeline's Extracellular-Domain Structure — and a ChEMBL Lead Out-Scores It There
abstract: Pakistan has the highest age-standardised diabetes prevalence in the world — 34.5 million adults, 9.3 million of them undiagnosed — and the GLP-1 receptor agonists that treat it are all injected peptides. Orforglipron is the first oral, non-peptide, small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist to complete phase 3, and it binds a pocket in the upper helical bundle that only partly overlaps the peptide site. We asked whether a standard automated docking pipeline ranks it correctly. Using the LeadForge protocol (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → Vina 1.2.7), we docked orforglipron and five ChEMBL leads on the pipeline's auto-picked structure, 4ZGM — the isolated extracellular domain with a semaglutide peptide fragment — and then re-docked the same compounds on 6XOX, the cryo-EM structure of GLP-1R bound to orforglipron itself. On 4ZGM, orforglipron ranks first at −7.66 kcal/mol; on 6XOX it scores −10.8, a 3.14 kcal/mol pocket effect, and the ChEMBL lead CHEMBL6167455 out-scores it at −11.3. The two structures' rankings correlate only moderately (Spearman rho 0.8, with the winner changing), and the correct pocket also ranks the measured potencies better (rho 0.7 on 6XOX, n = 5, versus 0.2 on 4ZGM, n = 4) — though the measured values span only 1.6-fold (EC50 0.012–0.019 nM), a band no docking screen can resolve finely. Rigid docking can re-dock orforglipron into its own pocket, but the auto-picked structure under-prices every compound by ~3–4 kcal/mol and can crown the wrong winner. The falsifiable next step is a cAMP assay of the same set: if the 6XOX rank predicts the EC50 rank and the 4ZGM rank does not, automated GLP-1R docking must use the cryo-EM pocket, not the best-resolved X-ray structure.
summary: Pakistan has the highest age-standardised diabetes prevalence in the world — 34.5 million adults, 9.3 million of them undiagnosed — and the GLP-1 receptor agonists that treat it are all injected peptides.

title: The 260-Metre Ceiling: A Falsifiable Attribution of Lahore's November Smog Peak to Domestic Sources and Seasonal Meteorology, with a Smog-Budget Policy for Punjab
abstract: Question. Is Lahore's November smog peak driven mainly by polluted air crossing the border from India, or by domestic emissions amplified by the seasonal collapse of the atmosphere's mixing height? Claim. The November peak is driven predominantly by domestic emissions — transport, domestic crop-residue burning, waste burning, industry and brick kilns — amplified by the collapse of the mixing height from 830–860 m in May–June to about 260 m in November, a ~3.2-fold compression of the air available to dilute the same emissions. Transboundary inflow is a secondary contributor, estimated at 13–30% across published studies. Falsifier. The claim would be refuted if a November smog episode showed (i) PM2.5 rising faster in border cities than in inland cities, while (ii) HYSPLIT back-trajectories showed air masses reaching Lahore from the east, and (iii) TROPOMI NO2 columns at the border exceeded Lahore's. The 8–10 November 2026 Diwali episode tested all three conditions and produced the opposite pattern: inland cities (Faisalabad, Multan) rose by 85 µg/m³ against 36 µg/m³ in border cities, Delhi air stayed at least 266 km from Lahore, and Lahore — not the border — is Punjab's strongest TROPOMI NO2 hotspot (92.31 µmol/m²). Identification. Natural experiment (the Diwali window as an exogenous transboundary shock) with a spatial gradient (distance from the border as the dose). Not an RCT; no single-source causal effect size is estimated. The paper falsifies the transboundary-dominant hypothesis; it does not prove exact domestic shares. One clean number: 260 metres — Lahore's November mixing height, the ceiling under which a city of ~14 million people breathes. The stakes number is 3.9 years: the average life expectancy air pollution removes from a Pakistani, up to 7 years in Lahore. Keywords: Lahore smog; PM2.5; mixing height; Sentinel-5P TROPOMI; source apportionment; transboundary air pollution; Punjab; khilafah; smog budget.
summary: Question. Is Lahore's November smog peak driven mainly by polluted air crossing the border from India, or by domestic emissions amplified by the seasonal collapse of the atmosphere's mixing height? Claim.

title: Four Captopril Stereoisomers Dock Within 0.07 kcal/mol on VIM-2 While Their Measured Potencies Span 76-Fold: Rigid Docking Is Blind to the Stereochemistry That Defines MBL Inhibition
abstract: VIM-2 is a B1 metallo-beta-lactamase that hydrolyses almost all beta-lactams including carbapenems, and no clinically useful inhibitor exists for it. The best measured inhibitor in the reference set, taniborbactam (Ki 0.02 µM), cannot be docked by AutoDock Vina at all because it contains boron, which Vina's PDBQT parser rejects — a tool limit the standard pipeline run for this paper hit and could not pass. The testable question that remains is whether rigid docking can resolve the potency gap between stereoisomers of the same molecule: D-captopril inhibits VIM-2 at 0.072 µM, L-captopril at 4.4 µM, and the two epi-isomers at 5.5 µM each, a 76-fold range from a single stereocentre flip, with crystal structures showing different binding modes. We docked all four stereoisomers with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on 4C1E, the 1.40 angstrom VIM-2 structure co-crystallised with D-captopril. The scores are minus 6.16, minus 6.19, minus 6.12 and minus 6.19 kcal/mol — a total span of 0.07 kcal/mol, thirty times smaller than Vina noise, with rank correlation against measured potency of 0.15. The screen cannot see the stereochemistry that defines this inhibition. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay IC50 comparison of the four stereoisomers on VIM-2 with a metal-aware rescoring of the same poses: if the measured 76-fold gap reproduces while every rescoring still ties them, the failure is confirmed as a scoring-function limit, not a pose-sampling error.
summary: VIM-2 is a B1 metallo-beta-lactamase that hydrolyses almost all beta-lactams including carbapenems, and no clinically useful inhibitor exists for it.

title: Nintedanib Tops a PknB Docking Rank That Matches Measured Potency Exactly: Two Approved Cancer Kinase Inhibitors and the Mitoxantrone Caveat
abstract: PknB is an essential serine/threonine kinase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and no PknB inhibitor has reached the clinic: the best published inhibitors are nanomolar in vitro and only micromolar against whole cells. We docked five compounds with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on 3ORK, the 1.60 angstrom structure of the PknB kinase domain (L33D mutant) with an ATP-gamma-S analogue in the ATP site: nintedanib, two matched-pair aminopyrimidine/pyrazole inhibitors from the same series, sunitinib, and mitoxantrone, the literature PknB inhibitor. The docking rank matches the measured potency rank exactly (Spearman rho 1.0, n = 4): nintedanib, Kd 3.6 nM, docks at minus 9.70 kcal/mol; the matched pair, Ki 13 and 17 nM, at minus 8.66 and minus 8.30; sunitinib, Kd 87 nM, at minus 8.24. Mitoxantrone, which has no attached PknB potency number and is excluded from the correlation, docks worst at minus 7.19 and carries a PAINS alert with the maximum Tox21 read-across for the DNA-damage assays SR-ATAD5 and SR-p53. Two approved cancer kinase inhibitors top a tuberculosis kinase ranking, and the literature inhibitor is the weakest and the most toxic — a clean repurposing signal and a warning in the same table. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay PknB kinase comparison of the four ranked compounds with a whole-cell assay on Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv: if nintedanib again measures most potent on the enzyme but fails on whole cells, the gap is confirmed as permeability, not potency.
summary: PknB is an essential serine/threonine kinase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and no PknB inhibitor has reached the clinic: the best published inhibitors are nanomolar in vitro and only micromolar against whole cells.

title: Cilomilast Out-Scores Roflumilast on PDE4D Despite a 171-Fold Potency Gap, and Crisaborole Cannot Be Docked at All: Rigid Docking Misses the Contact Points That Define PDE4 Inhibition
abstract: Phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) is the target of four approved drugs — roflumilast, apremilast, crisaborole and difamilast — and a 2025 structural study proposed a simple rule for their potency: roflumilast preserves all three active-site contact points (metal-ion site, conserved glutamine, water network), apremilast two, crisaborole one, and the measured IC50s follow the rule (0.7 nM, 0.14 µM, 0.24 µM). We docked the three dockable drugs with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on 3G4L, the 2.5 angstrom human PDE4D structure co-crystallised with roflumilast. Cilomilast, the weakest of the three docked by 171-fold, scores best at minus 9.62 kcal/mol; roflumilast scores minus 9.14 and apremilast minus 8.93. The 171-fold potency gap between roflumilast and cilomilast is 0.48 kcal/mol in the wrong direction, and the rank correlation against measured potency is 0.5 (n = 3). Crisaborole, the third drug in the comparison set, cannot be docked at all: it is a benzoxaborole, and Vina rejects boron — the second boronate this run has failed to dock, after taniborbactam on VIM-2. The screen cannot see the contact points that define PDE4 potency, and it cannot see the boronate that defines the class's newest chemistry. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay PDE4D IC50 comparison of the four drugs with a metal-aware rescoring of the same poses: if the measured 200-fold range reproduces while every rescoring still ties them, the failure is confirmed as a scoring-function limit, not a pose-sampling error.
summary: Phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) is the target of four approved drugs — roflumilast, apremilast, crisaborole and difamilast — and a 2025 structural study proposed a simple rule for their potency: roflumilast preserves all three active-site contact points (metal-ion site, conserved glutamine, water network), apremilast two, c…

title: MRTX1133 Re-Docks at −12.71 kcal/mol on the KRAS G12D Switch-II Pocket and Sotorasib Scores Worst: A Corrected Docking Benchmark After a Wrong-Target Pipeline Run
abstract: KRAS G12D is the commonest KRAS allele, driving about 42% of KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancers, and it has no approved inhibitor: the covalent KRAS G12C drugs cannot work because G12D has no cysteine to bind. MRTX1133 is the first non-covalent, selective KRAS G12D inhibitor, with a pERK IC50 of 2 nM in AGS cells, but the standard pipeline run for this paper resolved the target to the wrong enzyme and docked it into the wrong pocket, so both numbers from that run are discarded here and the correction is documented in full. We docked MRTX1133, three analogues from the same discovery paper, and the G12C inhibitor sotorasib as a negative control with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 on 7RPZ, the 1.3 angstrom KRAS G12D structure co-crystallised with MRTX1133 in the switch-II pocket. MRTX1133 re-docked at minus 12.71 kcal/mol; the analogues scored minus 11.62, minus 11.13 and minus 9.34 against measured pERK IC50s of 24, 530 and 24 nM; sotorasib scored worst at minus 7.74, as a G12C drug should on G12D. Rank correlation against measured potency is moderate (Spearman rho 0.65, n = 4), but two compounds with identical measured potency differ by 2.28 kcal/mol in docking, and the re-dock sits 2.52 kcal/mol clear of its own second pose. The screen ranks the series roughly right and cannot resolve equal potencies. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay pERK comparison of the four Wang-series compounds in one KRAS G12D cell line: if compounds 25 and 36 again measure identically while docking differs by more than 2 kcal/mol, the gap is confirmed as a scoring artefact, not a potency signal.
summary: KRAS G12D is the commonest KRAS allele, driving about 42% of KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancers, and it has no approved inhibitor: the covalent KRAS G12C drugs cannot work because G12D has no cysteine to bind.

title: Ibrutinib Re-Docks at −10.86 kcal/mol on Its Own BTK Structure, but Four Sub-Nanomolar Covalent Inhibitors Score Worse: Rigid Docking Cannot Price the Cys481 Bond
